Facilities Manager – Data Center

The Role

The Facilities Manager leads a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technicians, contractors, and service providers responsible for maintaining highly available, mission-critical data center infrastructure.

This position oversees daily facilities operations, maintenance programs, capital projects, vendor performance, safety, compliance, and operational risk. The Facilities Manager drives operational excellence through continuous improvement, sustainability initiatives, strong technical governance, and proactive asset management.

Key Responsibilities

Critical Facilities Operations

  • Lead the day-to-day operation of all critical data center infrastructure.
  • Ensure the availability and reliability of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, security, and life-safety systems.
  • Maintain compliance with Service Level Agreements, operational standards, and uptime objectives.
  • Oversee 24/7 operational support, including incident response, escalation, and recovery.
  • Ensure Standard Operating Procedures, Emergency Operating Procedures, and Methods of Procedure are accurate, current, and consistently followed.
  • Review and approve high-risk maintenance activities and changes affecting critical infrastructure.
  • Support capacity planning and ensure infrastructure can meet current and future operational requirements.

Leadership and Team Management

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Critical Facilities Engineers and Technicians.
  • Manage shift schedules, staffing levels, technical training, competency assessments, and performance evaluations.
  • Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and development plans.
  • Foster a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Coordinate contractor and vendor activities to ensure work is completed safely, on time, and to the required quality standards.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, and retention of facilities personnel.

Maintenance and Asset Management

  • Develop and oversee preventive, predictive, condition-based, and corrective maintenance programs.
  • Manage maintenance planning, scheduling, work orders, and equipment records through the Computerized Maintenance Management System.
  • Ensure maintenance activities are properly risk-assessed, documented, approved, and communicated.
  • Monitor equipment condition and lifecycle performance and develop repair, upgrade, and replacement strategies.
  • Ensure maintenance activities minimize operational risk, service disruption, and unplanned downtime.
  • Review recurring equipment failures and implement long-term corrective actions.
  • Maintain accurate asset registers, maintenance records, technical documentation, and spare-parts inventories.

Infrastructure Management

Oversee the operation and maintenance of critical systems, including:

  • Medium-voltage and low-voltage electrical distribution systems
  • Uninterruptible Power Supply systems and battery plants
  • Standby diesel generators
  • Automatic Transfer Switches
  • Switchgear, transformers, protection systems, and electrical panels
  • Chillers and chilled-water systems
  • Computer Room Air Handling and Computer Room Air Conditioning units
  • Air Handling Units
  • Pumps and hydronic systems
  • Heat exchangers
  • Building Management Systems
  • Data Center Infrastructure Management systems
  • Fire detection and suppression systems
  • Security and access-control systems
  • Fuel storage and distribution systems
  • Water-treatment and leak-detection systems

Health, Safety, Environmental and Regulatory Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with the French Labour Code, applicable EU directives, French environmental regulations, local requirements, and company policies.
  • Maintain a strong health, safety, and environmental culture across the facility.
  • Manage Permit to Work, Lockout/Tagout, electrical isolation, hot-work, confined-space, and contractor-safety programs.
  • Ensure employees and contractors hold the appropriate training, authorizations, and certifications for their assigned work.
  • Lead incident, near-miss, and equipment-failure investigations.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis and ensure corrective and preventive actions are completed.
  • Prepare for and support regulatory inspections, customer assessments, insurance reviews, and internal and external audits.
  • Ensure appropriate emergency-response plans, drills, and escalation procedures are maintained.

Capital Projects and Commissioning

  • Support the planning and delivery of infrastructure upgrades, replacements, expansions, and capital projects.
  • Review technical designs, specifications, risk assessments, and commissioning plans.
  • Coordinate project work with operations teams to minimize risk to live services.
  • Participate in factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, and integrated systems testing.
  • Ensure complete operational handover, including training, asset documentation, test results, warranties, and as-built drawings.
  • Monitor project budgets, schedules, risks, and contractor performance.

Financial and Vendor Management

  • Develop and manage the facilities operating and capital budgets.
  • Forecast maintenance, staffing, utility, equipment-replacement, and service-contract costs.
  • Review maintenance contracts, statements of work, and service-level agreements.
  • Monitor vendor performance against established service levels and key performance indicators.
  • Conduct regular vendor-performance reviews and implement improvement plans when required.
  • Support the procurement of equipment, spare parts, technical services, and facility-related contracts.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency without compromising safety, reliability, or compliance.

Sustainability and Energy Management

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
  • Monitor Power Usage Effectiveness, energy consumption, water consumption, and carbon-related performance.
  • Support sustainability programs and environmental reporting requirements.
  • Work with engineering and operations teams to optimize cooling, electrical loading, and equipment performance.
  • Evaluate energy-saving initiatives while protecting system reliability and redundancy.

Operational Reporting

Track, analyze, and report key operational metrics, including:

  • Infrastructure availability
  • Preventive maintenance completion
  • Corrective-maintenance backlog
  • Mean Time to Repair
  • Mean Time Between Failures
  • Power Usage Effectiveness
  • Energy and water consumption
  • Capacity utilization
  • Incident and alarm trends
  • Vendor performance
  • Safety performance
  • Budget performance

Prepare accurate operational reports and recommendations for senior leadership and relevant stakeholders.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Building Services Engineering, Facilities Management, or a related technical discipline.
  • A master’s degree is advantageous but not required.
  • Equivalent technical education combined with substantial relevant experience may also be considered.

Experience

  • Minimum of seven years of experience in critical facilities, mission-critical operations, industrial facilities, or a comparable technical environment.
  • At least three years of experience leading technical teams, contractors, or service providers.
  • Experience in hyperscale data centers, colocation facilities, hospitals, power generation, manufacturing, utilities, or other continuously operating facilities is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience managing critical maintenance activities and operational risk.
  • Experience managing budgets, vendors, maintenance contracts, and capital projects.

Technical Knowledge

Strong working knowledge of:

  • Critical electrical infrastructure
  • Medium-voltage and low-voltage distribution
  • UPS systems, batteries, standby generators, and transfer systems
  • HVAC and mission-critical cooling systems
  • Chilled-water and hydronic systems
  • Building Management Systems

  • Preventive and predictive maintenance practices
  • Equipment lifecycle and reliability management
  • Risk assessment and root-cause analysis

Preferred Qualifications and Certifications

  • Degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering.
  • Appropriate French electrical authorization under NF C 18-510, such as B0/H0V, B1V, B2V, BR, BC, H1V, H2V, or HC, depending on the responsibilities assigned.
  • Sauveteur Secouriste du Travail certification, or equivalent workplace first-aid qualification.

  • France Chimie/UIC N1 or N2 safety training, or equivalent site-safety qualification, where required by the facility.

Join us as Delivery Manager!

We’re looking for a proactive, solutions-driven Delivery Manager to lead and scale our growing team of 20 grant specialists. You’ll own day-to-day delivery, ensuring tasks are completed on time, proposals meet the highest quality standards, and blockers are resolved quickly. You’ll build effective processes across grant prospecting, writing, and submission, while coaching and developing your team, optimising workflows, and using AI-powered tools to improve efficiency without compromising quality.

As Delivery Manager, your mission will be to:

  • Manage a growing grant writer team of 20 people.

  • Ensure the team completes their backlog of tasks each day.

  • Ensure that there are no overdue tasks (unless they absolutely cannot be completed that day).

  • Ensuring that all blockers are communicated effectively to the product/engineering team.

  • Establish blind QA reviews across delivery pods to maintain high proposal standards.

  • Own recruiting, onboarding, performance evaluations, and promotion tracks for the grant writers, providing direct coaching on complex mechanisms like federal NOFOs, logic models, and multi-year program budgets.

  • Monitor pipeline density across all 400 accounts to smooth out deadline clustering, reallocate overflow work across pods, or deploy a vetted bench of contract writers during peak funding cycles (e.g., Q2/Q4 deadlines).

  • Standardize narrative frameworks, boilerplate language libraries, AI-assisted research tools, and submission workflows to shorten drafting cycles without compromising personalization.

  • Partner with the Head of Client Success to define realistic production timelines, enforce submission milestones, and serve as an escalation buffer to protect writers from scope creep and unvetted, last-minute client requests.

  • Manage hiring; interviewing grant writers, onboarding them, and ramping them up.

  • Own reporting; producing weekly reports around grant writer delivery and blockers/ bottlenecks to our leadership team.

This role is a perfect match for you if you have:

  • At least two years of experience managing large teams doing repetitive tasks.

  • Experience working in the impact/nonprofit space with specific knowledge of the grant writing process.

  • Managing knowledge economy workers.

  • A strong university degree/education.

title: Developer Support Engineer (London)
descriptionHtml:
About the company

Braintrust is the agent observability platform. By actively applying intelligence to agent traces and automatically surfacing the most critical patterns, Braintrust gives teams the visibility to understand how agents behave in production and the tools to improve them.

Teams at Notion, Stripe, Box, OpenAI, and Cloudflare use Braintrust to trace their agents, find the issues in their observability data, and run evals that tell them how to improve.

About the Role

At Braintrust, surprisingly good developer support is one of our most important strategic advantages. Our customers are developers building LLM-powered applications, and they move fast. We win by helping them move faster.

We’re looking for Developer Support Engineers — both mid-level and senior — who are obsessed with helping developers overcome challenging technical blockers to achieve their goals. You’ll troubleshoot issues, identify workarounds, ship fixes, and document your findings to help future developers move faster.

This role blends technical problem solving, developer empathy, and tight collaboration with Engineering, Solutions, and Product. If you love solving complex problems, explaining technical concepts clearly, and making developers’ lives easier, we’d love to talk with you.

This role will be remote based in London.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve API and SDK use issues alongside customers codebases (Python or TypeScript).

  • Reproduce customer-reported bugs, identify likely causes in our codebase, and collaborate with Engineering to resolve them.

  • Own support communications with developers using Braintrust — primarily via Slack and email — and build trust through clear, technical, and empathetic communication.

  • Write and maintain knowledge base documentation that turns unknowns into knowns, unblocking future developers.

  • Identify opportunities to improve the developer experience, including tools, documentation, and support workflows.

  • Write scripts, fix bugs, and contribute to internal tooling that enhances the support process.

  • Capture and relay customer feedback to Product and Engineering, helping shape roadmap priorities.

  • Participate in on-call rotations, responding to critical customer issues or providing coverage during local holidays.

  • Provide technical mentorship to cross functional peers and guide support processes and escalation handling.

  • Develop and champion opinionated stances on improving developer experience and product reliability.

 

What we're looking for

  • Experience supporting developer-facing products as a Software Engineer, Customer Engineer, Developer Success Engineer, Technical Account Manager, or similar customer facing technical role.

  • Can write, debug, and reason through Python and/or TypeScript codebases.

  • Are comfortable learning and reasoning about APIs, SDKs, and developer tools quickly.

  • Take personal ownership of technical problems and follow through until customers are unblocked.

  • Communicate clearly, empathetically, and effectively — especially when explaining complex or confusing issues.

  • Are insatiably curious about use cases for LLMs and excited to support tools that make AI more measurable, reliable, and trustworthy.

 

Bonus Points For

  • Experience supporting developer tools, ML infrastructure, or observability platforms.

  • Familiarity with OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar LLM APIs.

  • Comfort working with datasets, evaluation metrics, or prompt engineering.

  • Experience contributing to support tooling, documentation, or product-led growth initiatives.

  • Have been a senior technical team member or tech lead in a high-growth environment, taking ownership of ambiguous technical scenarios.

  • Have submitted PRs to production codebases to fix customer-impacting issues in backend services, SDKs, or infrastructure.

  • Hold cloud certifications or equivalent experience troubleshooting containerized environments (e.g., Terraform, Kubernetes).

 

Why join Braintrust

  • Build a culture of care, learning, and mutual support together

  • Solve challenging, unknown technical issues faced by developers

  • Pave the way for future developers and peers to benefit from your experience

Benefits include

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Daily lunch, snacks, and beverages

  • Flexible time off

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Wifi & cellphone stipend

Equal opportunity

Braintrust is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

title: Directeur.rice des Finances
descriptionHtml:
283 – Directeur.rice des Finances

Premier opérateur public européen de traitement et de valorisation des déchets, le Syctom, l’agence métropolitaine des déchets ménagers, est un acteur majeur de l'économie circulaire et de la ville durable.

Au service de 81 communes franciliennes et de près de 6 millions d'habitants, le Syctom accomplit sa mission de service public avec pour objectif de faire des déchets une ressource.

Une mission exigeante qu'il conduit grâce à ses 145 collaboratrices et collaborateurs et 7 apprenti.es, en lien étroit avec les collectivités adhérentes (Ville de Paris et 10 Etablissements publics territoriaux du Grand Paris) en charge de la collecte des déchets et l'ensemble des acteurs de la filière.

Le budget annuel s’élève à 822 M€ et le Plan des Investissements 825 M€ d’ici 2030.

Le Syctom traite et valorise chaque année 2,2 millions de tonnes de déchets ménagers dans ses unités de traitement innovantes (3 unités de valorisation énergétique - UVE -, 5 centres de tri, 2 centres de transfert et une future unité de Biométhanisation). Le patrimoine du syndicat, alliant performance industrielle et exemplarité environnementale, est exploité sous contrat par des entreprises privées ou des SemOp présidées par un.e élu.e du syndicat.

Acteur responsable et innovant, le Syctom est engagé en première ligne dans la dynamique de transition écologique française. Il accompagne le développement de la collecte des déchets alimentaires, développe des solutions de traitement et de valorisation, agit en faveur de la réduction et du tri des déchets et s’engage dans la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre (GES) liées à ses activités de transport et de logistique.

La Direction générale adjointe Ressources et moyens (DGARM) pilote les moyens financiers, humains, informatiques, juridiques et logistiques ainsi que du fonctionnement de l’institution et des actions œuvrant à la qualité de vie au travail. Elle accompagne les directions opérationnelles au quotidien, pilote des processus et démarches collectives et participe au projet stratégique de la collectivité, qui définit des orientations communes afin que le Syctom accompagne au mieux le territoire dans ses ambitions de développement durable.

Acteur clé de la performance et de la soutenabilité financière du Syctom, la Direction des Finances assure le pilotage des ressources financières de l’établissement. Elle accompagne les projets stratégiques de la collectivité en apportant son expertise en matière de planification et d’ingénierie financière, de construction budgétaire, de tarification et de financement des investissements, dans un environnement institutionnel, réglementaire et économique contraint et en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de structuration et de modernisation de ses fonctions ressources, le Syctom mène actuellement un audit stratégique visant à renforcer la fonction financière et à développer une culture de pilotage et de contrôle de gestion. Celle-ci vise à consolider les capacités d'analyse et d'anticipation de l'établissement, à développer une culture de pilotage de la performance et à renforcer les outils d'aide à la décision au service de la Direction générale et des élu.es.

Missions

Sous la responsabilité du Directeur général adjoint Ressources et moyens, vous pilotez la définition et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie financière et budgétaire de la collectivité. Le budget 2026 s’élève à 479 M€ en fonctionnement et 343 M€ en investissement. Le montant de la contribution acquittée par les collectivités membres du syndicat est de 268 M€.

A partir d’hypothèses que vous coordonnez et documentez en lien avec les directions opérationnelles, vous réalisez des prospectives financières pluriannuelles. Dans ce cadre, vous êtes chargé.e de structurer un dialogue de gestion budgétaire qui permette d’optimiser les moyens financiers du Syctom et de piloter au plus juste le montant de redevance acquittée par les collectivités membres. Vous proposez un cadrage financier et pilotez les processus et calendriers budgétaires en lien avec les directions opérationnelles.

Dans le cadre de la feuille de route, vous êtes force de proposition et préparez, sous la responsabilité de la Direction générale, les travaux et décisions des élu.es quant à la trajectoire financière et tarifaire du syndicat. Vous conduisez les analyses financières en vue de déterminer les risques et opportunités à court et long termes, et proposez des scénarios à la Direction générale. Vous construisez et pilotez des indicateurs financiers clés et proposez des outils d’aide à la décision pour la Direction générale et l’exécutif, en développant le SI décisionnel financier.

Avec une dette de près d'un milliard d'euros, vous définissez et proposez à la Direction générale une stratégie de financement à long terme garantissant la soutenabilité financière des projets du syndicat. Vous supervisez la gestion active de la dette, de la trésorerie, des recettes et des financements externes.

Vous assurez également le pilotage financier du patrimoine industriel du Syctom et accompagnez la définition des trajectoires financières nécessaires au financement des charges futures induites par les investissements structurants, notamment en matière d'amortissements, de fiscalité et de coûts d'exploitation des nouvelles installations.

À ce titre, vous apportez une expertise de haut niveau en matière de fiscalité locale et de fiscalité des activités industrielles. Vous pilotez les démarches d'optimisation et de sécurisation des charges fiscales du syndicat et contribuez à la mise en place de processus et d'outils fiabilisés, en lien avec les directions techniques, patrimoniales et d'exploitation.

Le Syctom s’est engagé dans la création de SemOp pour l’exploitation de ses sites, dans le cadre de marchés publics. Vous participez activement à la mise en place des moyens de suivi et de contrôle financier de ces structures pour le compte du Syctom, en lien avec la gouvernance et les équipes qui qui en assurent la maîtrise technique et le contrôle des contrats. Vous assurez également le suivi des structures desquelles le Syctom est actionnaire (Semardel, Sigeif Mobilités).

Vous accompagnez la Direction générale dans le dialogue financier avec les collectivités adhérentes et contribuez à la pédagogie des enjeux financiers du syndicat auprès des élu.es et partenaires institutionnels tels que les établissements bancaires ou les agences de notation.

Dans un contexte de transformation de la fonction financière, vous encadrez une équipe et participez à des projets structurants visant à renforcer les outils de pilotage et le contrôle de gestion, avec l’opportunité de contribuer directement à l’évolution de l’organisation, des pratiques et des processus du syndicat.

Ce poste offre ainsi l'opportunité de contribuer directement à la transformation financière du premier acteur public européen du traitement des déchets ménagers, dans un environnement conjuguant enjeux industriels, financiers et environnementaux de premier plan.

Profil

De formation supérieure (Bac+5) en Finances publiques, vous disposez d'une expérience réussie en direction ou en pilotage financier et budgétaire d’un organisme public.

Vous détenez une expertise dans le domaine de la préparation et l'éxécution budgétaire comme dans la stratégie financière. Aguerri.e aux outils et processus associés, vous savez également les faire évoluer dans une perspective d'amélioration continue, et détenez une appétence pour les questions organisationnelles.

Vous avez une vision stratégique des enjeux financiers et budgétaires d’une collectivité, et avez la capacité à synthétiser et proposer une feuille de route et des options à des fins d'aide à la décision pour la Direction générale.

Pédagogue, réactif.ve et proactif.ve vous savez impulser et mener un dialogue de qualité avec les directions opérationnelles. Vous savez porter un projet et aider à la décision. Vous faites preuve de qualités managériales, d’un excellent sens relationnel et avez le goût du travail collaboratif et en équipe.

Recrutement par voie statutaire (cadre d’emplois des attaché.es ou administrateur.rices territoriaux.iales 1er grade) ou, à défaut, contractuelle (CDD de droit public).

Poste à pourvoir en janvier 2027.

Le Syctom est investi dans l'accompagnement des collaborateur.rices reconnu.es travailleur.ses handicapé.es.

Dans le cadre de sa démarche en faveur de l’égalité professionnelle et de la diversité, le Syctom s’engage contre toute forme de discrimination.

Le Syctom :

Facilite l’organisation des temps :

  • Forfait cadre

Participe aux frais :

  • de télétravail avec l’allocation forfaitaire de télétravail (aux montants maximum permis dans la fonction publique)
  • de restauration : accès au Restaurant Inter Entreprise du siège du Syctom (prise en charge du Syctom à hauteur de 7,26 €) et attribution de tickets restaurant pour les jours de télétravail (d’une valeur de 12,10 €).

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals is seeking an imaginative physician drug developer, with the flexibility and confidence to work across diseases within the neurology and hematology therapeutic area.  This role includes the opportunity to provide clinical leadership in developing RNAi therapeutics in Alnylam’s expanding portfolio, which spans from rare genetic to common diseases.

The successful candidate’s primary role will be one of the clinical study leads working on the plasminogen program transitioning from Phase 2 to Phase 3. The Director will report directly into the program clinical development strategy lead who provides the clinical research oversight of the program. The Director is expected to play a leading and influencing role in the overall clinical development strategies and drive progress and operational excellence of his/her clinical trial(s). This work will also involve extensive consultation and collaboration with external experts. The Director, Clinical Research, will work in a matrix organization across Regulatory, Biostatistics, Clinical Operations, Preclinical, Commercial & Quality Assurance teams to ensure fully harmonized and integrated development strategies. title: Director of Cloud Infrastructure & Security
descriptionHtml:
Vestiaire Collective is the leading global platform for desirable pre-loved fashion and a pioneer in transforming how people consume fashion. Our mission is simple: make circular fashion the norm, not the exception.
Through technology, expertise, and a highly engaged global community, we enable millions of people to buy and sell fashion in a more sustainable way. Founded in Paris in 2009, Vestiaire Collective is now a globally scaled marketplace with offices in Paris, London, Berlin, New York, Singapore, and Ho Chi Minh City, and logistics hubs across Europe, Asia, and the US. Today, we are a team of around 600 people from over 50 nationalities, united by a shared ambition: to drive meaningful change in the fashion industry. Our values, Activism, Transparency, Dedication, Greatness, and Collective, shape how we build, collaborate, and grow every day.

About the Role:

Vestiaire Collective runs a global marketplace on AWS and GCP — Kubernetes, Kafka, Terraform, Vault, Cloudflare, Datadog, a large PHP application under active modernisation, a series of microservices in different tech stacks (Goland, PHP, Node) and a fast-growing surface of AI-powered services.

As Director of Cloud Infrastructure and Security, you will lead a small team of six senior individual contributors across Cloud Infrastructure (DevOps/SRE) and Security. This is a hands-on Director role: alongside setting the strategy and roadmap, you will work directly with the team on architecture, technical decisions, incidents and delivery. You will be accountable, alongside Product Development teams, for the reliability, cost-efficiency and security posture of everything we run in production.

What you will do:

Leadership across two teams

  • Directly lead, develop and retain a small team of six (6) experienced engineers across Cloud Infrastructure and Security. This is a player-coach role without multiple management layers, so you will remain close to the team’s technical work and day-to-day priorities.

  • Define a joint roadmap for both teams, aligned to business priorities and risk appetite, and make explicit calls on what we will not do.

  • Establish clear KPIs, SLOs and risk metrics, and report regularly to leadership on reliability, cost and security posture.

  • Set the operating model: what product teams self-serve behind guardrails versus what your teams own centrally.

  • Foster a culture where reliability and security are shared accountabilities, not tickets thrown over a wall, including establishing a Security Champions model across engineering.

Cloud infrastructure, reliability and platform

  • Own our AWS and GCP footprint end to end: EKS, networking, secrets (Vault), data stores (RDS/Aurora, MSK, ElastiCache, MongoDB Atlas, OpenSearch) and the edge (Cloudflare).

  • Establish real reliability engineering practice: SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, and a business continuity plan.

  • Drive infrastructure-as-code maturity: Automating Terraform change application, advancing our move to GitOps (ArgoCD), and enforcing guardrails at creation time with policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) so provisioning is safe, self-serve and reviewable.

  • Consolidate observability into a single source of truth for metrics, logs and traces.

  • Improve developer experience and delivery throughput: CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), paved roads, test environments on demand, and delivery metrics that hold up.

  • Own FinOps: infrastructure cost per unit of business value, cost accountability pushed back to each team, and continued run-rate reduction. Cost discipline is a first-class objective.

  • Support the modernisation of our core platform: Tech migrations, runtime and framework upgrades, and continuous database and Kubernetes upgrades.

  • Attack toil systematically: automate the recurring requests, and hand safe self-service back to product teams rather than absorbing the work.

  • Grow the foundations for AI-augmented engineering and operations

Security

  • Own security strategy and posture across cloud, application, identity, detection and response, building and improving the governance: risk register, published roadmap, remediation SLAs, and a recurring reporting cadence for leadership.

  • Strengthen cloud security posture management (CNAPP) and secure-by-default configurations across all environments.

  • Improve Embedding security into the SDLC and CI/CD: establish full static-analysis and dependency-scanning coverage with clear criteria for when critical findings block a release.

  • Mature vulnerability management, penetration testing and our bug bounty program into one prioritised program with SLAs and aging reports that measurably reduce risk.

  • Advance identity and access management toward least privilege and zero trust: automated provisioning from groups, and periodic access reviews.

  • Mature logging, detection and incident response, closing SIEM coverage gaps

  • Set guardrails for safe AI adoption (shadow AI outside approved paths, data and prompt leakage, prompt injection, model abuse) and defend against AI-enabled fraud and phishing.

  • Ensure compliance with GDPR, PCI DSS v4, NIS2, and CIS v8, including a maintained, reusable evidence library rather than evidence gathered on request.

  • Collaboration with legal and finance teams on compliance and forensic investigation topics

  • Manage third-party and supply-chain risk with vendor tiering and a recurring review cadence.

  • Own the security-built services your team already runs (back-office authentication and ACL, banning/fraud tooling, phone verification) and decide what to keep, hand over or retire.

  • Own endpoint security and partner closely with Corporate IT on device and identity coverage.

  • Keep security awareness and training relevant to a threat landscape that now includes AI-enabled social engineering.

Who you are:

  • 8+ years with a Significant experience in Infrastructure, Platform Engineering, DevOps, SRE or Cloud Security, including experience leading engineers.

  • You may currently be an Engineering Manager, Senior Engineering Manager or Head of who is ready to broaden your scope and step into a first Director role.

  • Strong practical experience with public cloud, ideally AWS, Kubernetes and Infrastructure-as-Code, with the willingness to remain close to architecture, incidents and technical delivery.

  • Track record establishing reliability practice at scale — SLOs, incident management, on-call, capacity planning, disaster recovery.

  • Demonstrable cloud cost optimisation / FinOps results at meaningful scale.

  • Strong grounding in cloud and application security fundamentals — IAM, network security, secrets management, CSPM, OWASP Top 10 — and the judgement to know when to hire the depth you don't have.

  • Working knowledge of compliance frameworks (GDPR, DORA, PCI DSS, NIS2) and how to turn requirements into practical controls.

  • Experience leading through incidents and security events under pressure.

  • Excellent communication skills: able to make a technical trade-off legible to a CFO and a risk decision legible to an engineer.

  • Comfortable operating with a lean team — ruthless prioritisation, automation over headcount, pragmatism over perfection.

Our Tech Stack includes:

  • AWS cloud (primary), GCP, Kubernetes, Vault, Cloudflare, Datadog, ArgoCD, Okta. Applications are built on top of PHP 8, Golang and Node.js, using MariaDB, MongoDB and Kafka.

What We Offer

  • Purpose-driven work at scale
    Join a company reshaping the fashion industry towards circularity, you directly contributes to reducing waste and extending the life of luxury items.
  • High-impact scope & ownership
    Work on products used globally, where your decisions have immediate, measurable impact on millions of users across 70+ countries.
  • A truly international environment
    Collaborate with a diverse team of 50+ nationalities across Paris, London, Berlin, New York, Singapore, and Ho Chi Minh City.
  • Career acceleration in a fast-moving scale-up
    Take ownership early, grow fast, and shape your path, as an expert or a future leader.
  • Learning & growth as a priority
    Dedicated budget, continuous feedback culture, and opportunities to work on cutting-edge topics (AI, marketplace dynamics, scalability, etc.).
  • Flexible ways of working
    Hybrid model (typically 2 days remote per week), with trust and autonomy at the core of how we operate.
  • Give back through action
    2 paid days per year to support a cause of your choice and actively contribute to positive impact beyond your day-to-day role.
  • Competitive compensation & benefits
    Including bonus, health coverage, lunch vouchers, Gym-Pass, and additional legal perks depending on your location.

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds including women, people with disabilities, and other marginalized communities, are less likely to apply unless they meet 100% of the criteria.

At Vestiaire Collective, we believe diversity drives better decisions, stronger products, and more meaningful impact.
If this role excites you but your experience doesn’t align perfectly, we still encourage you to apply, your perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

Vestiaire Collective is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

PS: We take candidate experience seriously, and your safety too !

  • Contact you via WhatsApp, Telegram, or similar platforms
  • Ask for payment or banking information at any stage of the process

title: Director of Data Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Working at WGSN
Together, we create tomorrow


A career with WGSN is fast-paced, exciting and full of opportunities to grow and develop. We're a team of consumer and design trend forecasters, content creators, designers, data analysts, advisory consultants and much more, united by a common goal: to create tomorrow.


WGSN's trusted consumer and design forecasts power outstanding product design, enabling our customers to create a better future. Our services cover consumer insights, beauty, consumer tech, fashion, interiors, lifestyle, food and drink forecasting, data analytics and expert advisory. If you are an expert in your field, we want to hear from you.

About the Role

We're hiring a Director of Data Engineering to own WGSN's data platform: its architecture, its data models and how it runs day to day. You'll report to our Group Chief Data Officer, lead a team of five data engineers, and work closely with our Group Technology, Data Science and programme teams.

At the heart of the role is the trend spine, the connected backbone that links trend signals, taxonomies, forecasts and content. Next year we launch an expanded social data product across TikTok, Reddit and Instagram, and after that we plan to rebuild the platform. You'll lead both, and lay the data foundations for the AI products that will sit on top.

What You'll Do

  • Own data architecture and modelling across the WGSN platform
  • Design and build the trend spine
  • Integrate structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, from social and search signals to runway imagery and proprietary research
  • Lead, develop and set standards for a team of five engineers, plus agency and contractor partners
  • Lead architecture discussions with our Group Technology team
  • Shape the planned platform rebuild, including stack, cost and vendor decisions
  • Introduce AI-assisted and agentic engineering practices and build AI-ready data foundations
  • Make sure the platform is reliable, well governed, GDPR compliant and cost effective

What We're Looking For

  • Experience designing or substantially reshaping a data platform, with clear ownership of architecture and modelling decisions
  • The technical depth and confidence to lead engineering and architecture conversations with senior technologists
  • Data engineering leadership at a small to mid-size business, or at manager level in a larger organisation with real design ownership
  • Hands-on experience with semi-structured and unstructured data alongside structured data
  • A practical track record of using AI to change how your team builds

Nice to Have

  • Snowflake, Databricks and AWS
  • Embeddings, vector search, feature stores or knowledge graphs
  • Taxonomy or ontology design
  • Social, web-scale or licensed third-party data
  • A background in media, information services, SaaS or e-commerce

Experience

Around 10 or more years in data engineering, with at least four years leading engineers.

title: Director of Product, AML & Fraud Prevention
descriptionHtml:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

At Vinted we are devoted to making second-hand the first choice worldwide. Vinted Pay is the regulated payments entity that makes it possible through enabling Vinted users to spend money, receive money, keep money and payout, while keeping them safe from financial crime.

We are establishing a new AML & Fraud Prevention product domain within Vinted Pay. As a regulated financial institution operating across Europe, our obligations grow as we grow: anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing controls, sanctions screening, KYC, transaction monitoring are protecting our members and our balance sheet from fraud and other illegal activities. Today these capabilities sit across several teams and tools. This domain will own them end to end, and turn financial crime prevention into a mature product: controls that satisfy regulators without adding friction for the honest majority.

This is a newly created domain. As its leader you will work with your functional peers (Engineering, Data, Design) to assess the status quo and construct the long-term vision. You will be responsible for setting domain goals, delivering on already identified opportunities, hiring, and executing the product vision.

You’ll report to the leader of Engineering/Product/Design/Analytics at Vinted Pay, and partner with Product Directors across Vinted Pay and the wider marketplace, as well as with our Compliance, Legal, Risk, Risk Operations, Engineering, Design and Analytics functions.

In this position, you’ll 

  • Drive and align the AML & Fraud Prevention domain on a single, unified vision, expressed through measurable objectives and key results
  • Own the product roadmap across AML/CTF, sanctions and PEP screening, KYC, transaction monitoring and fraud prevention, build alignment across product teams, cross-functional partners and the leadership
  • Partner with our MLRO, Compliance, Risk and Legal teams to translate regulatory obligations into product requirements and make the case for automated solutions where manual controls are in place
  • Manage multiple competing objectives and provide clarity to the delivering organisation 
  • Use and analyse data to size risk, identify product opportunities, and build the right capabilities at the right time
  • Own build-vs-buy decisions, then assess and collaborate with the vendors in building and maintaining AML/Fraud prevention solutions
  • Get ahead of regulatory change: the EU AML package and AMLA, PSD3/PSR, evolving sanctions regimes, rather than reacting to it
  • Build, mentor, lead and scale a team of Product Managers
  • Implement best in class product development and managerial practices

About you 

  • 7+ years of experience in product management, with a substantial part of it in AML, financial crime, compliance, risk or fraud, ideally at a regulated financial institution, e-money institution, PSP, bank or fintech
  • 4+ years of developing people and managing teams, including Product Managers
  • Deep working knowledge of the AML domain: KYC and identity verification, customer risk scoring, sanctions and PEP screening, transaction monitoring and alert handling, SAR/STR reporting, and the regulatory frameworks behind them (EU AML directives and the AML package, national transpositions, FATF standards)
  • Hands-on experience with fraud and scam prevention: detection models and rules engines, account takeover controls, chargebacks and disputes, and the trade-off between loss reduction and false positives
  • A proven track record of successful product launches (at least two substantial projects with a 6–9 month minimum duration)
  • Comfortable operating in a regulated environment: you have worked alongside compliance officers, internal and external auditors and supervisors, and you know how to move quickly without creating regulatory exposure
  • Able to deliver from 0 to 1, and not afraid to build your own tools to achieve your goals
  • Exceptional leadership skills and substantial experience building high-performing teams of 10+, ideally not only in product (and we’d expect your former teams to still be singing your praises!)
  • Strong business judgement, analytical skills and long-term planning skill
  • Both quantitative and qualitative: able to assess and understand complex systems quickly, to integrate usability studies, research and market analysis into product requirements, and to be a product ambassador to the rest of the organisation
  • Well organised, with a collaborative attitude and a strong sense of ownership
  • An excellent communicator, including in written and spoken English

Work perks 

  • The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme
  • 25 days of paid annual leave
  • Newest MacBook models
  • Digital mental and emotional health support and Employee Assistant Program (EAP)
  • Frequent team-building events
  • Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture
  • Lunch benefit per working day
  • Access to a discounted gym membership plan
  • A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted
  • Comprehensive Medical Insurance

Working at Vinted 

Individual Learning Budget

We invest in your professional growth! As part of our commitment to continuous learning, we offer an annual learning budget to support your personal and career development through courses, certifications, workshops and more.

Hybrid Work 

We’ve adopted a hybrid workplace model where 2 days in the office are recommended but not enforced. It’s up to you and your team to decide on the exact days you’ll spend working together in person.

The Vinted Group is committed to building an inclusive workplace where people from all walks of life feel a sense of belonging. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and life experiences. title: Director of Self Serve
descriptionHtml:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.


The Role

Self-serve today represents a meaningful part of Paddle's revenue. This role owns the commercial mandate to grow that significantly. Not just to run self-serve, but to build the strategy for where and how it scales, and execute against it.

We're hiring a Director of Self-Serve to take full commercial ownership of Paddle's self-serve motion, running and scaling it as a business line. Self-serve is a material and fast-moving part of our revenue, and it needs an owner who thinks in unit economics, not just funnel metrics.

You'll set the strategic direction, and work across Finance, Product, Engineering, Demand Generation, Partnerships, and RevOps to align everyone behind it. Getting this right is a genuinely cross-functional endeavour, and your ability to bring people with you will be just as important as your commercial acumen.

You'll operate with a small, focused team including engineering capacity. This is a role for someone who wants to build and run the engine hands on, not manage through layers.


What you'll do

Own the line. Carry the commercial number for self-serve end to end, from acquisition through adoption, to revenue and net retention. Own the unit economics, and how they improve.

Set the strategy. Form a clear commercial view of where self-serve creates value, ensure Finance and Product alignment, and translate it into a plan the business can execute against.

Own activation and time-to-value. Evolve who and how we onboard through self-serve, how we nurture them through lifecycle stages, and the in-product experience that gets them to value fast. Increasing volume while decreasing time-to-value, not trading one for the other. You fundamentally approach the self-serve experience as a product, running structured discovery and experimentation, not defaulting to only marketing levers.

Shape the demand. Define the customer profile that makes the economics work and work collaboratively with Demand Generation on the targeting you need, co-owning a single funnel against a shared ICP.

Orchestrate cross-functionally. Codify the work into clear streams with clear owners, influence the Product, Engineering, and Risk roadmaps, and run a regular business cadence that keeps people aligned on priorities and impact.

Deepen partner integrations. Work hand-in-glove with Partnerships to turn distribution relationships into deep well-integrated channels, owning the commercial outcome of partner-sourced volume.

Build and run the engine. Design and run the experimentation, tooling, and tracking to improve funnel codification, time-to-value, activation, and conversion using AI where it raises velocity and quality, applied to the right customer. As the motion scales, you'll shape the team around it.

Make the economics stack up. Working closely with finance you own self-serve pricing and packaging as a lever, to ensure profitable scale.


How you operate

Go get the answer yourself. When something doesn't add up, you pull the data, run the analysis, and don't wait to be handed a conclusion. Self-reliance is core to how you operate, not a fallback when support isn't available.

You interrogate, not just observe. Live the ‘five whys’ principle, with the ability to take a plausible looking number, trend, signal and stress-test it until you've found the actual driver, not the first explanation that fits. You default to hypothesis and experiment before you default to opinion or output, treating the funnel as something to be iteratively shaped, not just optimised within.

Given a mission, you don't let go of it. You have a real hunger to find and unlock value you believe is there, working through blockers, organisational, technical, or data.


We'd love to hear from you if you are

  • Deeply experienced in a PLG or self-serve motion in a high-growth tech business, where you've built and owned the funnel rather than a sales-assisted or enterprise motion, and have been accountable for the number, not adjacent to it.

  • A commercial operator who has owned a revenue line, channel, or segment. Someone who operates in founder mode with the instinct to understand the economics, not just the funnel beneath them.

  • You think like a product manager: prioritizing ruthlessly, scope experiments tightly, and see the boundary between growth and product as something to work across.

  • Fluent at moving from data to a commercial conclusion, with the discipline to separate signal from noise and turn analysis into a clear decision rather than a list of observations.

  • A sharp critical thinker who interrogates the brief rather than taking it at face value, challenges assumptions (including ours), and is as willing to conclude "this isn't where we should be investing" as to confirm the plan.

  • A genuine cross-functional leader who has brought structure to messy, multi-team programmes, influenced roadmaps you don't control, and run the cadence that holds a programme together.

  • A credible presence in front of senior stakeholders up to executive level; you communicate with clarity and authority and can take a room with competing priorities to a clear decision.

  • Equally comfortable operating at altitude and dropping into the detail, and always coming back up with a point of view, not just findings.

  • Able to use AI pragmatically; dynamic onboarding, predictive scoring, real-time segmentation, as a means to commercial outcomes, not an end in itself.

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we're committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don't care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you're from. We're more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you'll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don't match every part of the job ad, especially if you're part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there's anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We're committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let's grow together.

Why you'll love working at Paddle

We're a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

  • Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

  • Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”

  • Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

Connecting at Paddle

We're a 'digital-first' company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

We recognise that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.

Our Paddle hubs:

  • In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub)

  • In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada)

  • In APAC: Singapore

descriptionHtml:

Within this organisation, the Velocity team owns the paved road for consumer app development across mobile and web: shared SDKs and client foundations, integration patterns and multi-brand customisation, migration playbooks and reference implementations, and developer tooling that makes building on shared foundations fast and safe. Our mission is to reduce the cost, time, and risk of building consumer experiences across platforms and brands. Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive platform, with AI agents that work alongside every team, from Finance to HR, to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.

Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally, passing $100M in ARR in 2026 and doubling revenue for the second year in a row. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake, and Siemens use Pigment every day to make better-informed decisions and navigate any scenario with confidence.

In October 2026, we raised a $250M Series E at a $2.3B valuation, bringing our total funding to $650M+. Today we’re a growing team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco, and Austin, and we’ve been named a Visionary in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software two years running.

At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you’re driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

You’ll join Pigment’s Reporting & Collaboration community, working as a senior hands-on Frontend Engineer on some of the most complex parts of the product.

This community is responsible for how users access, configure and interact with their data. That creates significant frontend challenges around large-scale datasets, filtering, visualisation, complex configuration and increasingly AI-powered experiences.


On the engineering part:
  • Spend approximately 80% of your time as a hands-on engineer, designing, building and shipping production features.
  • Work on complex, data-heavy frontend problems where performance, usability and scale all matter.
  • Build sophisticated interfaces for displaying, filtering and interacting with large datasets.
  • Work with React, TypeScript and JavaScript, while contributing to the wider technical decisions behind the product.
  • Partner closely with Product Managers, Product Designers and Engineers to take features from problem definition through to production.
  • Make pragmatic engineering decisions based on the needs of the product and its users, rather than pursuing technical complexity for its own sake.
  • Contribute to areas across Reporting & Collaboration depending on business needs and your interests, including data extraction and filtering, visualisation, complex configuration and emerging AI experiences.
  • Use modern engineering tooling, with Pigment teams working across GCP, CircleCI and AI development tools such as Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot.

    • This is not a traditional Engineering Manager role where you step away from the code. You will remain a senior individual contributor and be expected to ship.


    On the people management part, here is what it entails:

    At Pigment, people management and technical leadership are deliberately separated.

    Tech Leads lead the technical direction of individual teams. Engineering Managers focus on developing engineers as people while remaining hands-on engineers themselves.

  • Spend approximately 20% of your time on people management.
  • Gradually take on direct reports after establishing yourself as an IC during your probation period.
  • Coach engineers across different teams within the Reporting & Collaboration community.
  • Support engineers with career progression, development, feedback and performance.
  • Run regular 1:1s and help engineers understand what they need to do to progress.
  • Set clear expectations and provide actionable feedback.
  • Handle difficult performance conversations when necessary and follow through with clear development plans.
  • Partner with Tech Leads to understand how your reports are performing technically without taking ownership of the Tech Lead's responsibilities.
  • Help create an environment where strong engineers can continue to develop while doing their best work.

    • Engineering Managers typically support engineers across multiple teams within their community rather than "owning" a single engineering team.


    Who you are

    We’re looking for someone who is both a strong senior Frontend Engineer and an experienced people manager.

  • Significant professional software-engineering experience, with the technical depth expected of a senior engineer.
  • Strong recent hands-on frontend engineering experience.
  • Production experience with React, TypeScript and/or JavaScript.
  • Previous formal people-management experience. Ideally, you have already managed engineers rather than looking for your first management opportunity.
  • Experience owning areas such as coaching, career development, feedback and performance management, not simply mentoring engineers or leading projects.
  • Experience building complex product interfaces, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics, data platforms or another sophisticated data-heavy product.
  • Experience solving frontend problems involving areas such as large datasets, visualisation, filtering, configuration, performance or complex workflows.
  • A strong product mindset. You care about what you're building, who is using it and whether it genuinely solves their problem.
  • Strong collaboration skills across Engineering, Product and Design.
  • The ability and desire to remain deeply hands-on in the code while managing people.
  • The autonomy expected of a senior IC: once you understand the problem, you can work with the team to move it forward without needing constant direction.

title: Engineering Manager, Guardian
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm.

Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products.

Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group.

About the Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow the Guardian team in London. You will own the engineering strategy and execution for production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users.

This is a builder-manager role with substantial technical depth. You will set direction, develop engineers, and create the operating cadence for a high-performing team, while remaining close enough to the work to shape architecture, review designs, debug difficult problems, and write code when it is the highest-leverage way to help the team move forward.

The role is highly visible and cross-functional. You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI.

This role is based in our London office.

In this role, you will

  • Lead, hire, and develop a London-based team of engineers working across agent safety, backend systems, applied AI, and product infrastructure.

  • Set the technical roadmap for Auto-review and the broader Guardian platform, balancing safety, product utility, latency, and operational reliability.

  • Build production systems that evaluate agent actions in real time, detect potentially harmful behavior, and support safe recovery or escalation paths.

  • Improve how oversight systems understand user intent, environmental context, permissions, and relevant personalization signals while protecting privacy and avoiding unnecessary friction.

  • Partner closely with alignment researchers to turn prototypes, evaluations, and new monitoring techniques into scalable product capabilities.

  • Work across Product, Security, Infrastructure, and other engineering teams to integrate Guardian capabilities into agent experiences throughout OpenAI.

  • Establish rigorous evaluation and operational practices, including adversarial testing, failure analysis, monitoring, and metrics for safety performance, false positives, latency, and user impact.


You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have significant experience leading engineering teams that shipped complex, high-stakes production systems end to end.

  • Have built with AI agents or large language models in a core product, startup, or technically serious independent project, and understand the unique challenges of agentic systems.

  • Bring strong product-engineering judgment and can navigate tradeoffs across safety, usability, speed, and reliability.

  • Can partner effectively with research teams, translate open-ended findings into engineering plans, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines.

  • Have a thoughtful management system for hiring, coaching, performance, and execution.

  • Care deeply about building AI systems that are useful, trustworthy, and safe.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Engineering Manager - Unified Platform
descriptionHtml:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the Team

The Unified Privacy Platform team’s mission is to earn the trust of every DoorDash user by upholding their right to privacy, consent, and transparency. We are building a common privacy foundation across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo so Consumers, Dashers, and Merchants can understand how their data is used, control their choices, and exercise their privacy rights through simple, consistent experiences.

Our work is organized around three connected pillars: the Privacy Center, a unified user-facing destination for privacy controls and rights; the Unified Privacy Platform, which captures and enforces consent, policy, jurisdictional requirements, and privacy actions; and Privacy Operations and Intelligence, which gives Legal, Support, Privacy, and engineering operators the workflows, diagnostics, audit history, and automation needed to resolve privacy work safely and efficiently. 

Together, these capabilities turn fragmented, one-off compliance work into reusable platform primitives that can support new products, brands, and emerging regulations.

Location: London, UK. This is a hybrid role, with 3 days a week in the office.

About the Role

DoorDash is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Unified Privacy Platform team. You will lead a team of backend and platform engineers responsible for the next generation of privacy and consent infrastructure, including the Privacy Center, the User Consent Platform, privacy-policy decisioning, self-service data-rights experiences, and the operational tooling required to manage privacy cases at global scale.

As the Engineering Manager, you will own and execute a multi-year vision for privacy at DoorDash. You will balance legal and regulatory correctness, user trust, security, reliability, and developer velocity while building systems that work consistently across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. You will be a strategic partner to Product, Legal, Security, Data Governance, Marketing and Communications, and engineering leadership, establishing clear ownership boundaries and turning complex privacy requirements into scalable, self-service capabilities.

What you'll be doing

  • Lead and mentor a high-performing team of backend and platform engineers, fostering a culture of ownership, privacy by design, operational excellence, and thoughtful cross-functional partnership
  • Drive the technical strategy across the Privacy Center, the Unified Privacy Platform, and Privacy Operations and Intelligence
  • Build the cross-brand User Consent Platform, including canonical consent state, policy and configuration management, consent SDKs, audit history, and consistent enforcement across products and jurisdictions
  • Deliver simple, self-service experiences for consent and communication preferences, Right to be Forgotten (RTF), Right to Information (RTI), and Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs)
  • Turn emerging privacy and regulatory requirements into standardized platform capabilities instead of one-off product implementations
  • Lead the migration from fragmented legacy consent systems to a single source of truth across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, while managing compatibility and safe deprecation
  • Define clear contracts with data-governance fulfillment systems and downstream product and storage teams so privacy actions are traceable, retryable, auditable, and correctly reflected back to users and operators
  • Provide architectural guidance for distributed systems that manage sensitive user choices, policy evaluation, orchestration, secure data delivery, reporting, and immutable audit trails
  • Partner with recruiting to build a diverse and inclusive team, attracting and retaining exceptional engineering talent

What You’ll Need to Thrive

  • A bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 3+ years of experience in people management leading backend or platform teams
  • 8+ years of industry experience
  • Extensive experience as an engineer or engineering leader in a fast-paced, platform-focused development environment
  • Proven experience designing large-scale distributed systems, service application programming interfaces (APIs), policy or rules engines, workflow orchestration, state machines, data-lifecycle systems, or audit architectures
  • Preferred experience with privacy, consent, data governance, or regulatory systems, including concepts such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), data-subject rights, retention, deletion, and legal holds
  • The ability to translate ambiguous legal, policy, and product requirements into clear platform boundaries, reusable abstractions, and executable roadmaps
  • Strong product sense and the ability to partner effectively with Legal, Product, Design, Security, Data, Marketing, Support, and engineering teams across multiple brands and geographies
  • A growth mindset—you are eager to expand your skills, raise the quality bar, and build enduring systems in a rapidly changing environment

Nearly 1 in 3 of Ashby’s globally distributed team call Europe home! We’ve landed over 1000 customers in EMEA representing ~23% of our global revenue base, with well over 100 in the DACH region, clear evidence of strong product-market fit. We’re doubling down our investment in the region with in-market GTM, CS and Support resources. EU Data Residency and product localisation are committed and coming soon. We believe there is a meaningful opportunity to help modern teams move beyond legacy recruiting software.

Ashby replaces 3-5 tools in a consolidation & efficiency play that’s equally loved by recruiters and CFOs. We’re known as a clear AI-leader in the recruiting space. We are rapidly extending from a best-in-class recruiting product toward a multi-product platform, expanding upmarket, into new industries, and internationally. For sales reps, that means a large market full of legacy tools, and a product portfolio that creates room for both new business and expansion. This is a chance to participate in how a category-defining company wins in its next phase of growth.

We are equally intentional about how we build the business. We have established a remote-first, high-performing sales organization that rewards learning and accountability. We use data to set achievable quotas, and reward sustained impact with competitive compensation and meaningful upside. We prioritize coaching and career development, with AEs advancing to Enterprise & Leadership roles in just a few years — 38% of the team who have been here more than a year have been promoted or taken on a new role!

You will work with people who care about craft, customer outcomes, and winning together—without sacrificing the trust, autonomy, and balance required to do your best work over the long term. Don’t just take my word for it, see what the team has to say about working here.

About this Role

TA tools in the Enterprise represent a huge market opportunity, a $1B+ TAM, and the incumbents are legacy players. We are displacing a collection of tools (ATS, Sourcing & CRM, Scheduling, Analytics, Offers & Approvals) with a consolidated talent suite. This is a proven playbook that Workday used to win the HCM market as customers realize value in a multitude of ways.

We are seeking a German-fluent and Germany-based Enterprise Account Executive to help us win Enterprise (1,000+ employees) accounts by managing the full sales cycle from pipeline generation through to closed-won.

In this role, you'll focus on new logo acquisition. Our emphasis is on your ability to excel in the areas listed below and your appetite for continuous growth & improvement.

  • 📣 You demonstrate mastery of clear communication. You ask questions with precision and can explain complex concepts in simple terms.

  • 🎯 You are proactive in identifying and pursuing new business opportunities, and comfortable sourcing >50% of your own pipeline. You're both resourceful and innovative in finding new business opportunities.

  • 💻 You can confidently deliver micro-demos before engaging your SE partners. You can't imagine not being fluent in the product you sell.

  • 🎧 You are highly skilled at discovery. You believe in preparation to establish a point of view, and through discovery validate or refine your perspective to identify a project's business drivers aligned to executive priorities.

  • 🤝 You have strong business acumen. You quickly connect the dots between technical problems and their downstream business impacts. You craft compelling business cases with this context.

  • ⚔️ You're adept at competitive or evangelical selling in new or established markets.

  • 🏔️ You skillfully guide prospects through the evaluation—engaging the right stakeholders at the right time to create consensus for a strategic technology decision.

  • 🤓 You enjoy becoming an expert and tailoring discussions to address each prospect’s unique challenges.

  • ⚡️ Your peers describe you as action-oriented and persistent. You're always on the leaderboard for outbound effort and pipeline created.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You write and send crisp follow-up emails, on time. You also take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates. (We use HubSpot, Gong, Chili Piper and Apollo.)

  • ✈️ You are willing to travel at least 25% of the time for customer engagements and events.

Requirements:

  • 🤝 You have 5+ years of full-cycle closing experience and have closed many >$100,000 ACV opportunities

  • 📢 You have experience selling complex platform technologies in a sales-led GTM motion

  • 📈 You are a new business hunter and are confident in your abilities to self-source >50% of your own pipeline

  • 🌍 You have sold to multiple regions within EMEA and have strong written and verbal fluency in both English and German

  • 🇩🇪 You are based in Germany

Bonus Points:

  • 🤝 You have experience selling to Talent or People leaders

You shouldn't apply if:

  • 💼 You're more of a relationship builder who focuses on selling into the install base and aren't excited about a new business focused role.

  • 💻 You believe that "tech stuff" is the SE's job. Our AEs all develop product acumen while SEs are a partner in our team selling motion.

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough — we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

descriptionHtml:
Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ?

Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Tu prends en charge les sujets les plus complexes remontés par nos utilisateurs et nos équipes Support.

Tu peux venir de différents environnements : cabinet d’expertise comptable ou éditeur de logiciel comptable.

  • a déjà travaillé sur des sujets complexes nécessitant analyse et coordination ;

  • est à l’aise avec les outils et problématiques techniques ;

  • sait communiquer clairement avec des interlocuteurs métiers et techniques ;

  • parle anglais dans un contexte professionnel, à l’écrit comme à l’oral ;

  • fait preuve de rigueur, d’autonomie et de curiosité.

title: Extrusion & Process Technician or Extrusion Engineer (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
About Humify GmbH

Humify is an innovative start-up developing a novel technology to convert biomass into valuable humic substances. Our mission is to improve soil fertility, support sustainable agriculture, and contribute to long-term carbon storage.

We are a small, international team of scientists and engineers working to bring this technology from the laboratory to industrial production.

The Position

We are looking for a hands-on person to support the operation, maintenance, and optimization of our small-scale extrusion equipment for biomass conversion.

You will work directly with our engineers and scientists to prepare experiments, operate the extruder, modify equipment, and ensure that our experimental processes run safely and reliably.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys practical technical work, solving mechanical problems, and experimenting with new technologies.

Your responsibilities

  • Equipment operation: Set up, operate, monitor, and maintain a laboratory- or pilot-scale extruder for biomass processing.

  • Experimental support: Prepare biomass feedstocks, conduct extrusion trials, collect samples, and document results.

  • Equipment assembly and modification: Assemble, adjust, and improve mechanical components, feeding systems, screw configurations, and other process equipment.

  • Maintenance and troubleshooting: Identify and resolve mechanical and operational problems, perform routine maintenance, and minimize equipment downtime.

  • Process monitoring: Monitor operating parameters such as temperature, pressure, screw speed, feed rate, and material flow.

  • Workshop activities: Support the construction of prototypes, installation of sensors, and modification of experimental equipment.

  • Documentation: Record operating parameters, maintenance activities, and experimental observations.

  • Safety and organization: Maintain a safe, clean, and well-organized technical workspace.

What you bring

  • Professional background as an extrusion technician, process technician, chemical engineer, or a comparable qualification

  • Practical experience in extrusion technology and process engineering, ideally within the chemical or environmental sector
