title: Field Marketing Manager
descriptionHtml:
The way companies innovate is broken. The systems built to create and protect ideas can’t keep up with the pace of change. Today, 90% of S&P 500 company value is intangible (e.g., in intellectual property) - yet R&D and IP teams spend half their time buried in manual work, sifting through patents and paperwork instead of pushing the frontier forward. The tools of creating and protecting are stuck in the past. We’re here to fix that.

Ankar is building the R&D tools for the AI era and defining what applied research will look like in the next 20 years. We’re building infrastructure and product experiences our customers rely on every day. You’ll translate messy, ambiguous problems into clean, dependable software—and you’ll do it at the cutting-edge of AI.

We’re at an inflection point:

  • We’ve raised >$24M to date from Tier-1 VCs like Atomico, Index Ventures, Norrsken, Daphni, and angels like the Founder of Hugging Face, CEO from Datadog, and Leaders from DeepMind and OpenAI.

  • We’re already working with the world’s most innovative companies including Fortune 500 company L’Oréal and global law firm Vorys

  • Expanding our world-class team with alumni from Palantir, Amazon, and BCG to tackle the $1T+ innovation market. We’re just getting started.

What you'll be doing

Own how Ankar shows up in the market - where we show up, what we do, and how we turn those moments into commercial outcomes. You’ll work closely with Sales and Commercial Development to build field programmes that create and accelerate pipeline.

  • Own Field Marketing end-to-end. Lead everything from industry conferences and webinars to executive dinners, roundtables and targeted experiences.

  • Build programmes around commercial priorities. Understand target accounts, active opportunities and pipeline gaps, and design programmes that create and accelerate demand.

  • Partner deeply with Sales. Drive target account selection, outreach, meeting generation and fast follow-up around every programme.

  • Build account-based experiences. Bring together events, gifting, direct outreach, digital and content to engage strategic accounts.

  • Execute brilliantly. Own logistics, vendors, speakers, stakeholders and timelines across multiple programmes.

  • Measure what matters. Track impact through account engagement, opportunities, deal progression, pipeline and revenue.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in B2B field marketing, owning and executing programmes from events and webinars to targeted account-based experiences.

  • Strong experience partnering with Sales to support target accounts, create pipeline and accelerate active opportunities.

  • Highly autonomous and comfortable managing multiple programmes, stakeholders, vendors and deadlines end-to-end.

  • Creative and commercially minded, with a strong bias towards action and measurable commercial outcomes.

  • Excellent communicator, able to work effectively across Sales, Marketing, leadership and external partners.

This role is not for you if...

  • You need a highly structured environment, a predefined playbook, regular working hours, or a schedule that never requires travel. We operate with high autonomy and ownership, expect our team to go above and beyond, be obsessed with our mission and thrive in ambiguity rather than wait for direction.

  • You prefer long planning cycles and certainty before acting. We move quickly, ship often, and adapt based on customer feedback and new information.

  • You want to manage the work rather than do the work. We're builders first, and everyone is expected to contribute directly to creating exceptional products.

  • You take it personally when ideas are challenged, priorities shift, or work gets redirected. We care more about finding the right answer than defending a particular one.

What we put behind our people

Building at the frontier takes exceptional people. We invest accordingly.

  • Health Insurance : Full private health & dental coverage for you and your dependents.

  • Pension: Flexible pension scheme with up to 5% employer matching on qualifying earnings.

  • Food on us: Team lunches twice a week, plus dinner when working late in the office.

  • Cycle to work: Green Commute initiative scheme (up to £3k) to help you get a new bike tax-free.

  • Way we work: We combine deep, in-person collaboration (3 days/week in our Shoreditch office) with flexibility and trust. What matters is ownership, impact, and results, not where you work from.

  • Visa sponsorship: Yes

title: Finance Systems Lead
descriptionHtml:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

The role

ElevenLabs runs a deliberately lean finance team across 10+ legal entities and 40+ countries. The stack is built around NetSuite, Stripe, Ramp, Deel, HiBob and Pigment, with a BigQuery/dbt warehouse underneath. We want a close where people review exceptions and agents handle the rest. You'll own that stack, from architecture and integrations to controls and vendors. This is a builder role, not a ticket queue.

  • Run NetSuite end to end. That covers multi-subsidiary setup, chart of accounts and segments, scripting and workflows, release management, and roles and segregation of duties as we build toward public-company controls.

  • Own the integration layer: Stripe, Ramp, Deel and HiBob into NetSuite, and NetSuite into the warehouse. Month-end should reconcile by design instead of by hand.

  • Lead selection and rollout of new systems, including usage-based billing and equity administration. You'll also handle the finance setup of every new entity.

  • Build with AI, alongside our Automations and Data teams. Examples include agents and automations for invoice coding, people-cost reconciliations and accounting requests.

  • Be the systems voice in finance decisions on new pricing models, new geographies and audit readiness.

Requirements

  • You've administered a multi-entity NetSuite OneWorld instance yourself, including SuiteScript/SuiteQL, saved searches, roles and releases.

  • You've owned an ERP or billing implementation or migration end to end, and you know how Stripe data flows into the ERP and into revenue recognition.

  • You build integrations, through iPaaS or code, that reconcile and alert when something breaks, and you're comfortable in SQL.

  • You understand R2R, P2P and O2C and the controls behind them, and you can work with accountants, engineers and auditors in the same week.

  • You work AI-first: tools like Claude Code or Cursor are part of your day, and you automate a workflow before you staff it.

  • Bonus: experience with Ramp, Pigment, Metronome or another usage-billing platform, Deel/HiBob, or n8n, or dbt/BigQuery; SOX or ITGC work at a pre-IPO or public company.

Growth Potential

We believe in hiring the best talent in the world to make an impact in the right role at the right time. At ElevenLabs, strong performance creates opportunities for growth. Here are some of the career paths you can expect after excelling in this role:

  • Lead a Finance Systems & Automation team as the company scales.

Location

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe, with the ability to operate in CET timezones required. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Warsaw and London.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Financial Analyst
descriptionHtml:
🏷️ Title: Financial Analyst

👫 Department: Analytics. Reporting to the Head of Analytics, working closely with our Co-Founder & CEO

💰 Salary: £60,000 - £80,000 + equity

🎁 Benefits & Culture: See here.

📈 Equity: A very generous EMI share offering.

🌴 Holiday: 26 days + bank holidays.

💗 Mission: Elevate later life for everybody and build the care sector of the future.

💻 Office Policy: Hybrid with a minimum of 2 core office days per week.

🌍 Office Location: London Bridge, London, UK.

 

🔍 The Opportunity:

Lottie is building the AI operating system for social care. Families find care through our marketplace. Care providers use Found to manage enquiries, occupancy and finances, with Eliza, our AI agent, answering family calls and chats on their behalf.

Lottie is growing fast. Care providers want what we're building, and we're heading into our next stage of growth. We need someone to get under the skin of the numbers, understand what's driving our success, and turn that into the plans, budgets and decisions that shape where we go next.

That's where you come in. You'll be the technical, commercially minded person at our CEO's side - writing the SQL, building the models and bringing the numbers that shape our biggest decisions. No middle man between the founder and the data: you go to the source yourself, work it out from first principles, turn it into a clear recommendation and then help make it happen.

With 2027 set to be Lottie’s most ambitious year yet, you'll own business planning and budgets, support investor relations and future M&A, and partner with teams across Lottie, including our commercial and marketing teams, to help them hit their goals. If you love both the data and the commercial story behind it, this is the role for you!

 

💻 What does this role involve?

  • Shape where Lottie goes next: Work directly with the execs on the biggest calls we make - pricing, where we invest, what we build - and own the analysis that decides them.

  • Sit at the heart of the business: Partner with Commercial, Marketing, Product, Ops and Finance to uncover what's really driving performance, and help each team act on it.

  • Own the financial model: Build and own the company's plans, budgets, forecasts and scenarios, track performance against them, and turn the variances into actions with the teams who own the numbers.

  • Board and investor numbers: Own the numbers for board packs and investor updates - clear, defensible and ready for scrutiny.

  • Turn insight into change: Take a question from analysis all the way to delivery, running it like a PM so the business actually moves.

  • Build, don't inherit: Use SQL, Python and AI to build the tools and processes a scaling company needs, from first principles.

💪 What problems will you be solving?

  • The data behind our success: Why is a new growth channel working so well, and how do we double down on it?

  • Pricing & unit economics: What drives margin in each product, and where pricing and packaging can lift it.

  • Board-ready numbers: Models, metrics and reporting that stand up to the scrutiny of investors.

  • M&A: Identify, evaluate and understand strategic acquisitions that accelerate Lottie growth.

  • Getting to the "why": Moving from what the numbers say to why they say it, and what we should do about it.

👀 We think you'll be a great fit if you…

  • Strong financial modelling: you can build a budget or forecast from scratch, read a P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, and turn it into a clear recommendation for Will. No FP&A title or accountancy qualification needed - a strong data or commercial background with real modelling depth is enough.

  • You are genuinely technical - you write your own SQL, work in git, are comfortable in Python and build financial models from scratch.

  • Work deeply with AI - you use tools like Claude every day to query data, build models and move faster.

  • Think from first principles and get quickly to how a business really makes money.

  • Can take a messy question, get to the data yourself and present a clear recommendation to a founder and leadership team.

  • Enjoy working closely with a founder - direct, curious and comfortable challenging up.

  • Are a builder, not just a modeller - you take a topic, run it like a PM and make it happen across the business at startup pace.

Sound like you but not quite 100%? Apply anyway - we're looking for potential and passion, not a perfect CV match.

 

💔 This role isn't for you if you...

  • Need someone else to pull the data. Here you write the SQL, build the model and own the answer.

  • Want to hand over a deck and walk away. We need someone who sees the decision through and makes the change happen.

  • Like analysis but shy away from action that comes from it. You'll be expected to make the call and defend it with the CEO and the leadership team.

  • Need a clear playbook and constant direction. Most of what you'll work on hasn't been done here before.

  • Want to stay in your lane. This role spans Growth, Product, Ops and Finance, often in the same week.

🔢 Lottie's Interview Process

  1. First interview with Lottie's Talent Acquisition Lead - 20 mins (remote)

  2. Interview with Will Donnelly, Lottie's Co-Founder & CEO - 30 mins (remote)

  3. Technical interviews - SQL, Python and financial modelling (using AI tools is encouraged)

  4. Final interview with Will Donnelly in Lottie’s office.

🤩 Candidate Experience:

  • Pre-Screen & First Interview: You'll receive an email notification, but no specific feedback will be provided at this stage.

  • Technical Interviews: If you are not successful after the technical stage, you'll receive constructive feedback via email and be offered a debrief call with our Talent Lead.

  • Final Interview: For final-stage candidates who are not offered the role, we will provide your feedback live via a phone call.

🚀 Meet Lottie

Founded with a mission to build the care sector of the future, Lottie is creating the AI operating system for social care - designed to unlock profitability for care providers and to make finding care as easy as booking a holiday on Airbnb.

Launched in London in July 2021, Lottie is widely recognised as one of Europe's fastest growing tech companies. Most recently, Lottie was the acclaimed winner of Deloitte Fast 50, LinkedIn Top Startups, The Sunday Times Tech 2026 and Startups 100.

As of today, Lottie offers three core products:

  • Lottie (B2B2C Marketplace) - Free service that helps families find the UK's best care homes and home care services.

  • Found by Lottie (B2B Vertical SaaS) - AI-native OS software supporting care providers to effectively manage their enquiries, occupancy and finances. Eliza by Found is our newest Found module: AI agents that handle care home enquiries - so no family goes unanswered. Launch video here.

  • Seniorcare by Lottie (B2B Vertical SaaS) - Employee benefit helping companies deliver outstanding eldercare support to their employees.

title: Fractional Data Privacy Specialist
descriptionHtml:
About us
Every large organisation runs on a web of legal entities, and the data behind them is scattered across in-house teams, law firms and accountants in PDFs, spreadsheets and slide decks. Jigsaw brings it into one place.
We started by giving lawyers and accountants a faster way to model client structures, and became the category leader doing it. Today 240+ organisations use Jigsaw, including all 10 of the world’s top 10 accountancy firms. Now we’re building Entity Lifecycle Management: one live record for every entity, from formation to dissolution.
Founded by former lawyer and repeat founder Stephen Scanlan, and backed by Exor Ventures.

Why join us:
You’ll help define a new software category with the backing of a loyal, global customer base. We hire people with high ownership and a bias for action, then trust them to do their best work.

About the role

You'll be Jigsaw's embedded data privacy advisor: the person product development and customer-facing teams turn to when a data or privacy question needs a real answer. This is a fractional role (starting at roughly 1-2 days a week in-office), working closely alongside our existing Legal team.

The focus for this role will be translating legal and technical complexity into commercially-focused, actionable responses to help free up teams to move quickly. In practice, this could be advising the product team on what compliance actions we need to take ahead of a new product release, making case-by-case decisions for customers with unique compliance requirements, or conducting analysis on customer DPAs ahead of a change to data processing locations, right through to how to answer a client's questions about our AI features.

This isn't a standardise-everything-and-leave role. We work with customers around the world in regulated industries (legal, financial institutions, accountancy and enterprises) with varying compliance needs, where one-size-fits-all templates aren't always an option and we need to adopt a flexible approach. The work here is genuinely ongoing, nuanced, and advisory rather than a project with an end date.


You'll get to...

  • Act as the go-to person for data and privacy questions across the business - in product meetings, customer rollout calls, and migration conversations

  • Turn specific customer contract terms into practical, commercial recommendations, weighing real risk instead of defaulting to "no"

  • Advise on cross-border and international data transfer questions, which come up constantly given our global customer base

  • Join customer calls to speak credibly with clients' own data privacy counsel, many of whom are lawyers or privacy specialists themselves

  • Translate complex legal and technical concepts clearly for non-legal, technical teams internally

  • Help build a genuine "privacy by design" culture at Jigsaw - getting privacy thinking embedded at the start of projects, not bolted on at the end

  • Spot opportunities to improve our templates, playbooks, and processes proactively, alongside the day-to-day reactive work

You'll need...

  • A working understanding of UK & US privacy laws, including UK & EU GDPR, the UK Data Protection Act and CCPA, ideally with experience applying them in a live commercial context, not just in theory

  • Genuine on-the-ground experience inside a tech company building product - this isn't a fit for a purely private-practice legal background

  • To be genuinely comfortable with cross-border and international data transfer questions

  • To be a commercial, pragmatic, solution-minded operator - someone who can weigh the significance and likelihood of a risk and propose a workable path forward, not someone who leads with compliance-first blockers

  • Excellent communication skills on two levels: credible and precise with legally sophisticated clients, and clear and accessible for non-legal internal teams

  • High ownership balanced with genuine collaboration, and able to build consensus

  • Comfort with a fractional working pattern - broadly protected days, with the pragmatic flexibility to handle something urgent (like a data incident) outside them

Nice-to-haves

  • Familiarity with other privacy frameworks, including AI governance or AI-related compliance questions

  • CIPP/E or CIPM certification

  • Experience working with clients in heavily regulated industries (law firms, accountancies, financial services)

  • Prior experience at a similar-stage scale-up with a broad base of regulated, legally sophisticated customers

Who should apply?

If you find the letter-of-the-law side of privacy the least interesting part of the job, and you're energised instead by being commercial, pragmatic, and embedded in a fast-moving business — this is for you. You'll get real autonomy and visibility across the company, working directly with product, engineering, and customer teams, rather than being buried in reactive, box-ticking compliance work.

title: General Counsel at amo
descriptionHtml:
amo is a Paris-based consumer social company. We want to build Europe's most ambitious consumer company. Our apps Bump and Sugar are used by millions of people all over the globe.

Location sits at the heart of one of our current products, and privacy, trust and safety are part of how we build, not an afterthought.

We're scaling fast, and this comes with legal implications. We want them handled in a way that speeds the business up.

The role:

We're hiring our first General Counsel to own amo's legal function end to end. This is a business role, not a support function: you'll work directly with the cofounders, join discussions from the start and work with every team, from Product and Distribution to People, Engineering and Finance.

You'll draft, negotiate and advise yourself on the topics that matter most. For everything else, you'll build and run a network of local counsel, with the right firm for each topic and each market, and turn their advice into clear decisions for the team.

How we think about legal:

At amo, legal starts from the product, to serve our users. We're not looking for someone who applies the rules by the book, but for someone who understands what we're building and why, and finds the legal approach that makes sense for it. You'll be judged on what you enable, not on how many memos you write.

  • Product and users first: you join discussions early and work with the team toward the same goal: making projects to life, fast and safe.

  • Pragmatic on risk: you know which rules are non-negotiable, where there is room for judgement, and how much risk is worth taking for the business. You give a recommendation, not a list of risks.

  • Built for scale: you set up the contracts, policies and processes that enable our growth.

What you'll own:

You'll cover every legal question that comes with scaling a consumer app across markets, working with the right local counsel on each topic:

  • Corporate: general corporate, group structure as we expand internationally, BSPCE plans and employee liquidity operations.

  • Employment: French labour law across the employee lifecycle, from contracts, immigration and internal rules to terminations.

  • Trademarks and IP: our global trademark portfolio: filing strategy, oppositions, watch services and disputes. Patents and content licensing as they come.

  • Compliance and data protection: GDPR, protection of minors, DSA, app store policies, and more. Regulator and law enforcement requests.

  • Commercial contracts: vendors and SaaS, partnerships, creator and influencer agreements, advertising, data processing agreements. Templates and a self-serve process so teams can move autonomously.

  • Litigation: pre-litigation and litigation across jurisdictions, with outside counsel. Clear risk assessments and options for the cofounders.

  • M&A: acquisitions and strategic transactions when the time comes, including due diligence, structuring and integration.

What success looks like:

  • Teams ship features, sign deals and expand without waiting on legal.

  • The cofounders spend far less time on legal: topics get tracked, briefed and closed without one of them driving each one, and nothing is discovered late.

  • The right local counsel is in place for each topic and market, on a budget we control.

title: Global Capability Centre UK Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Radiant

Radiant builds and operates AI-native cloud platforms for high-performance GPU workloads. Our infrastructure brings together data centres, compute, networking, storage and software to serve customers with demanding AI requirements.

As we grow internationally, we are establishing Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in several regions. These centres will provide specialist capability and operational support to teams across Radiant. We need a clear model for how each centre is launched, managed and connected to the wider business.

About the role

The Global Capability Centre UK Lead will help design, launch and scale Radiant’s GCCs. You will work closely with local GCC leaders and UK teams across People, Legal, Finance, IT, Security and Operations.

Your job is to make sure each centre has a defined purpose, an effective team structure, practical ways of working and the support it needs to deliver. You will also act as a point of contact and advocate for GCC leaders in the UK, helping resolve issues that span multiple teams or locations.

This is a hands-on, cross-functional role. You will help shape the overall model while also dealing with the details that determine whether a new centre works well from day one.

What you’ll do:

Plan and launch GCCs

  • Help assess potential locations based on talent availability, cost, time zones, regulation and operational needs.

  • Define the remit of each centre with local and UK leaders. Clarify which work belongs in the GCC, which stays with existing teams and how responsibilities may change as the centre grows.

  • Support launch plans, including the order in which centres and functions are established, key decisions, dependencies and transition milestones.

  • Coordinate with Legal, Finance, People and Security on entity setup, employment arrangements, data residency and other local requirements.

Build teams and operating models

  • Work with GCC leaders to design team structures, reporting lines and management layers that suit each stage of growth.

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition on headcount plans, hiring priorities and the skills needed to deliver each centre’s remit.

  • Align roles and career paths with Radiant’s global framework. Help local leaders plan for retention, succession and leadership development.

  • Define ownership, handoffs and escalation routes between GCCs and UK functions so work moves smoothly across teams and time zones.

  • Establish consistent core processes while adapting them where local law, customer requirements or operating conditions call for it.

  • Make sure onboarding, equipment, systems access and operational support are ready as teams join. Track time to productivity and address recurring blockers.

Connect GCCs with the wider business

  • Serve as the UK point of contact for GCC leaders, holding regular check-ins to surface risks, resolve issues and share good practice.

  • Bring together the right support from People, Legal, Finance, IT, Security and Operations when a centre needs a decision or intervention.

  • Help build effective communication and one Radiant culture across locations, while recognising the needs of local teams.

Manage governance and performance

  • Establish steering meetings and operating reviews with clear decisions, owners and follow-up actions.

  • Maintain a risk register for each centre covering people, delivery, security, compliance and commercial risks. Work with specialist teams on data protection, information security, export controls and local regulatory obligations.

  • Define useful measures for cost, hiring, productivity, retention, service quality and delivery. Report progress against each centre’s business case to Radiant leadership.

  • Identify when a GCC is ready to take on more complex or higher-value work, and help plan that expansion.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience building, launching, scaling or operating GCCs, shared service centres, delivery centres or similar international teams.

  • Strong experience in operating model design, organisation design and workforce planning. You can turn a broad plan into clear roles, processes and decisions.

  • Experience coordinating complex work across countries, cultures and functions, with the judgement to balance global consistency and local needs.

  • Commercial awareness and experience tracking budgets, business cases or operational performance.

  • Practical experience establishing governance, managing risks and working with specialist teams on international employment, security or compliance matters.

  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders and local leaders without relying on direct authority.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, comfort working in an evolving organisation and willingness to travel internationally.

Nice to have

Experience in technology, cloud or infrastructure businesses; setting up international entities or operating models; managing data residency or export control requirements; or supporting post-acquisition integration.

descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Opportunity

Deepgram is expanding into EMEA, and we're seeking a GM, Sales to own the region — building and leading the Enterprise and commercial segments of our Account Executive team, establishing Deepgram's European home in London, and driving growth across the region.

This role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll work with sales leadership to continue optimizing the systems, playbooks, and culture that scale ARR growth, while developing a high-performing team that converts opportunities into long-lasting customers. A core part of your mission is building Deepgram's next generation of sales talent through world-class training, coaching, and structured career development.

You'll partner closely with Marketing, Sales Leadership, RevOps, Customer Success, and Product to align pipeline strategy and leverage modern AI tools to boost productivity, personalization, and team efficiency. You will instill a culture of "Challenger" selling — teaching AEs how to disrupt legacy incumbents and lead with technical ROI.

  • Build the Ecosystem: Identify and sign strategic regional partners, GSIs, and local resellers to act as a force multiplier for Deepgram's direct sales efforts.

  • Operational Excellence: Implement rigorous forecasting, pipeline hygiene, and territory management across multiple countries, languages, and buying cultures. You will bridge the gap between London and our US HQ.

  • C-Suite Influence: Act as the primary executive sponsor for major regional accounts, navigating complex procurement cycles and technical AI evaluations.

You'll Love This Role If You

  • Thrive on building and scaling high-performing teams that consistently beat targets.

  • Want to build something from the ground up — including the office, the team, and the regional playbook.

  • Value working with tenured, high-caliber leaders who prioritize clarity, accountability, collaboration, and execution.

  • Enjoy blending data-driven sales operations with creative, human-centered leadership.

  • Are energized by developing AEs and building a culture of growth and continuous learning.

  • Believe in the power of AI to transform productivity, and are eager to harness cutting-edge tools to optimize performance.

  • Are passionate about Deepgram's mission to redefine what's possible with speech technology.

It's Important to Us That You Have

  • Experience: 12+ years in B2B SaaS sales, with 5+ years in a senior leadership role (Director/VP) covering EMEA — including the UK and at least one of DACH, the Nordics, France, or Southern Europe.

It Would Be Great If You Had

title: Growth Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

Growth is a critical function at Allica, sitting at the intersection of marketing, product, sales, and data. Our team is responsible for driving sustainable and scalable customer acquisition, engagement, and retention—ensuring our banking solutions reach and resonate with the right SMEs at the right time. Growth is both a science and an art. We blend commercial strategy with deep customer understanding, leveraging data to uncover new opportunities while ensuring every touchpoint aligns with Allica’s mission to empower established SMEs with the banking they deserve.

Role Description

The Growth Manager will play a key role in driving effective and sustainable growth across Allica's BRA customer journey — from onboarding through account activation and into deeper, embedded product usage. This role focuses on understanding customer behaviour end-to-end, identifying where customers stall or disengage, and building the strategies and capabilities needed to move them forward.

Using a data-driven approach, the Growth Manager will lead the design and delivery of initiatives that improve activation, engagement, and long-term customer value — often working with limited precedent and translating diagnosis into tools, frameworks, and ways of working that the wider business relies on. They will build alignment across marketing, product, sales, RM, and data teams, ensuring growth strategy is coherently applied across the customer journey.

This role is ideal for someone with strong applied critical thinking, a track record of leading initiatives with real ambiguity, and the ability to build stakeholder alignment without formal authority over the teams they influence.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Customer Behaviour & Cohort Analysis: Lead analysis of customer behaviour, lifecycle stages, and cohorts to identify key drivers of activation, engagement, and product usage, delving into complex problems to reach root-cause understanding rather than surface patterns.

  • Data-Driven Insights & Strategic Recommendations: Own the growth and engagement metrics that matter most for the customer journey, translating insight into strategy that shapes how the team and wider business operate.

  • Experimentation & Optimisation: Manage a robust experimentation pipeline, designing, prioritising, and overseeing tests across initiatives to ensure impactful, evidence-based decisions rather than one-off analysis.

  • Stakeholder Collaboration & Alignment: Build alignment across departments; marketing, product, sales, RM, and data, managing differing stakeholder expectations to keep initiatives progressing.

  • Framework & Capability Building: Take diagnosed problems through to operational reality, building the tools, scoring frameworks, and processes that other teams adopt and rely on.

  • Leadership & Ownership: Manage multiple objectives concurrently, ensuring accountability for outcomes even where the path forward isn't well precedented.

  • Communication: Design and deliver insightful, visually compelling presentations that influence decision-making and align stakeholders on growth strategy

Personal attributes & Experience

  • Experience working in hypothesis-led, problem-solving environments (e.g. high-growth start-ups, consulting or similar) is a plus.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to challenge assumptions and navigate complex, ambiguous problems using structured thinking.

  • Proven experience conducting complex data and performance analysis, ideally using SQL to work with large datasets.

  • Ability to translate customer and operational insights into clear, actionable changes across products, processes, or messaging.

  • Comfortable working with technical systems and integrations (e.g. CRM, analytics tools, automation platforms) to improve efficiency and scale.

  • High bar for quality while maintaining pace, particularly on work with limited precedent.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, able to influence and align teams with different priorities through clear, evidence-led recommendations.

  • Bias towards ownership and execution — able to independently drive work forward, frame problems, and recommend solutions with limited direction

 

Working at Allica Bank

At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:

  • Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

  • Options for flexible working

  • Regular social activities

  • Pension contributions

  • Discretionary bonus scheme

  • Private health cover

  • Life assurance

  • Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave

Don’t tick every box?

Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

Flexible working

We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.

We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

This exciting opportunity to join our passionate and enthusiastic team will take you to elite-level sporting events all around the world. As a member of our team, you will be responsible for delivering Hawk-Eye technology across a diverse range of current sports, including Athletics, Gaelic Sports, Volleyball, Horse Racing and Motorsports. title: GTM (DACH)
descriptionHtml:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

We are looking for an enthusiastic, driven, and proactive commercial analyst to join our expanding DACH go-to-market team. As a key member of our commercial team, you will play a crucial role in sourcing and qualifying leads, initiating outreach, and scheduling high-value conversations for our Account Executives. Your goal will be to create meaningful connections with healthcare practices and hospital groups, facilitating our mission to win across the DACH market.

This role requires a proactive mindset, excellent communication skills, and the ability to thrive in a high-growth startup environment. You will become an expert in engaging healthcare stakeholders, driving new opportunities, and contributing directly to the sales pipeline.

What you’ll do

  • Identify, research, and prospect potential customers and formulate go-to-market strategies

  • Execute inbound and outbound campaigns using a mix of calls, emails, social selling, and product-led signals to qualify leads.

  • Schedule high-quality meetings and product demonstrations for Account Executives, ensuring smooth handoff of qualified opportunities.

  • Own and manage end-to-end sales cycles for small SMB customers, from initial outreach through to closing deals.

  • Maintain accurate records in HubSpot CRM, manage and optimise sales pipelines, and consistently meet targets for qualified leads generated.

  • Collaborate closely with Account Executives, Marketing, Product, Operations, and Customer Success teams to streamline sales strategies and market positioning.

  • Stay updated on market trends, competitor activities, and evolving customer needs to identify new opportunities.

What we're looking for

  • 1-2 years of experience in sales or in tech, banking, consulting, PE/VC or similar.

  • Proven success in generating leads, qualifying prospects, and managing high-volume outreach campaigns.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, able to quickly build rapport and articulate the value of Heidi’s AI-driven healthcare solutions.

  • Highly organised, disciplined, and results-oriented with a strong problem-solving ability and the ability to prioritise multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Comfortable working independently in a dynamic, fast-paced startup environment with a high degree of accountability.

  • Eager to learn, adaptable, and excited about professional growth opportunities.

Attitude is more important than experience so if you are a hungry, competitive and highly motivated operator who has a knack for problem solving and building relationships we want to hear from you.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

title: Hardware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

The BMS is where software meets power. As our Hardware Engineer, you'll own the hardware side of the Anori BMS with a focus on the power stage: power electronics, cell connection and protection circuits. At the same time, you'll be our go-to person for hardware testing and make sure every board holds up under real-world conditions, from HiL test benches to stress tests and EMC pre-compliance. You'll work closely with Stefan, our CTO, and our firmware engineers to take the BMS from a tested prototype to a fully certified product. The technology is proven, the funding is secured, and the hardware decisions you make now will define how every future Anori BMS works.

Start date: from January 1, 2027

What You'll Do

  • Design and develop the power stage of our BMS: the highest power density on the market

  • Make the trade-off between performance, reliability, supply chain and price for each part

  • Build and run hardware tests: HiL setups, stress tests, HALTs and failure analysis

  • Plan and run EMC pre-compliance testing and prepare the path to conformity

  • Bring up new boards and debug them together with the firmware team

  • Contribute across the entire BMS hardware, wherever you are needed

What You Bring

Must have

  • Solid foundation in electrical engineering, from the schematic to the PCB. You know the parasitic effects of every practical circuit and you design with them

  • Deep knowledge of power electronics: MOSFET switch design, SOA, gate drive, current sensing and loss budgets

  • Experience with protection circuits, e.g. overcurrent, short circuit, over- and undervoltage, reverse polarity

  • Circuit and thermal simulation, for example in LTspice, with model-to-hardware correlation on the bench

  • Confident in the lab: oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads, thermal measurements and of course hand-soldering 01005 components

  • Critical, analytical, systematic thinking: you reason from first principles, make your assumptions explicit and challenge existing paradigms

Strongly preferred

  • A broad hardware skill set beyond the power stage: microcontroller circuits, analog sensing, communication interfaces (CAN, LIN, BLE, …)

  • Proven hands-on testing experience, including HiL tests and stress tests

  • Knowledge of DfM and new electronic manufacturing techniques, materials and general mechanical integration knowledge

  • Thermal design and cooling concepts for high-current paths

  • Wide-bandgap semiconductors and new switch topologies, and an interest to research and develop novel gate-drive techniques beyond standard drivers

Nice to have

  • High-voltage design above 60V: creepage and clearance, isolation, isolation monitoring and safe discharge

  • Experience with battery systems, cell connection and cell monitoring ICs (AFEs)

  • Test automation with Python

  • A background in safety-critical systems (IEC 61508, ISO 26262, …)

  • Knowledge in MBSE and requirements engineering methods (the skills, not the paper)

You don't tick every box? Apply anyway. No one matches a job description 100%. If this role excites you and you see yourself growing into it, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

  • Work on a product with purpose that redefines the state of art: our product is a key part to enable competitive battery energy storage.

  • Work directly with the founding team on decisions that shape the company. The team is small, so your ideas will matter. A lot.

  • Challenging engineering in an industrial, but research-near environment. We bring research into the industry.

  • A modern stack and methods: Rust, MBSE, everything as code, and the best tools and techniques for the job, chosen on merit.

  • To be both supported and challenged: room to grow, and the expectation that you will.

You might be a fit if

  • You hold yourself to a high standard and don’t settle for "good enough."

  • You want to have a big say in what the Anori BMS looks like and how it works

  • You are eager to try out new tools and enjoy incorporating AI into your work to make your life easier and more productive

  • You are excited about startups and all the opportunities and uncertainties that come with it

  • You want to be an active part in accelerating the energy transition in Europe

  • You are comfortable with English as a working language

  • You are happy to be in the office most of the time because for fast decisions we need to be in the same room. We expect you to be in the office at least 3 days / week

You also want to become an Anori? We cannot wait to meet you. Go and click the apply button. Don’t be shy, we are nice.

P.S. Extra bonus if you tell us what your favorite type of tea is.

title: Head of Applied AI
descriptionHtml:
Head of Applied AI

Location: Our offices are in Central London, along with several of our customers. Travel to our customer sites is required, the frequency of which will vary from customer-to-customer. You need to be able to travel onsite to London up to 3 days per week, although onsite requirements will vary week-to-week and customer-to-customer from 0 to 3 days.

Defence/SC Clearance Requirements:

SC clearance is required for our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance. DV clearance may be required for certain roles, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

About Cloudscaler

Cloudscaler is a rapidly growing cloud consultancy. We partner with ambitious enterprise and public sector customers to design, build, operate, and support secure, governed cloud platforms that meet the highest regulatory and industry standards.

We are scaling deliberately. Our revenue ambition depends on deploying the right people onto the right work quickly, and on making disciplined use of our capacity. This role is central to that.

 

About the role

Cloudscaler's Applied AI business unit launched at the start of 2026 and has grown quickly, with an established offering, live client engagements and a pipeline in place. The current Head of Applied AI is stepping back from the role for personal reasons and remains with the business to hand over, so the incoming Head inherits a running unit rather than a standing start. We are recruiting to take it into its next phase of growth.

The work is running; the structure is not yet. Offerings are defined, collateral exists, engagements are live and Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI is established. What does not yet exist is the shape around it: there is no ring-fenced team, no separate P&L and no formally defined roles. The unit began with strategy, technical expertise and sales all held in one place. Technical capability has grown since; strategy and commercial ownership have not. Formalising the practice - defining the team, the roles and the commercial structure - is part of the job rather than something the incoming Head inherits finished.

This role has both external and internal responsibilities:

Externally, it owns our AI go-to-market offerings and the customer, partner and pre-sales activity that turns them into pipeline, and it is Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI.

Internally, it carries full commercial accountability for the business unit, provides technical delivery oversight, builds and leads the practice, and is accountable for enabling the whole company to work with AI.

The role reports to the CTO and works closely with leadership across the business. The person needs to be technical enough to direct and challenge the engineering work, and commercially credible enough to scale the unit and its offering.

It is a hands-on role. In one week, you might write a business case for the Leadership Team, advise a client CTO on their AI strategy, review an engineer's architecture decision and speak at a conference on what we have learned.

External responsibilities

These responsibilities are customer-facing, partner-facing and public facing:

Relentless client focus - Maintaining a relentless client focus, calibrated to how mature the business unit is, and being decisive about where to concentrate effort and what to stop. Early on that means client meetings and pipeline growth; later it means shifting weight to larger, more sustainable areas of demand.

AI go-to-market offerings - Defining and owning our AI go-to-market offerings, working with sales to take them to market. For each offering, defining what it is, who buys it, the problem it solves, its indicative price and its delivery model, and reviewing the set as the market moves, retiring what no longer sells and evolving what does.

Customer relationships - Building trusted-advisor relationships with our customers, from CTOs and CDOs to engineering leaders, advising at every level and translating the same insight into the right language for a C-suite sponsor setting strategy and for the developers implementing it. Converting those relationships into repeat work and referenceable engagements.

Pre-sales leadership - Leading pre-sales activity on AI opportunities, from qualification through to proposal. Supporting the delivery and commercial teams on proposals, workshops and pitches, and leading on bids where applied AI credibility is the differentiator. Qualifying opportunities in or out, including declining those we should not pursue.

Client collateral - Developing reusable client collateral (opportunity assessments, roadmaps and business cases) grounded in real delivery experience. Keeping it current as the offerings and the technology move and making it available to the delivery and commercial teams rather than rebuilt for each deal.

Partner and industry relationships - Building and owning our AI partner and industry relationships (AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI and relevant industry bodies), including the technical relationship, joint go-to-market activity, and achieving and maintaining the respective AI partner competencies that matter to our customers. An existing network inside our partners is a significant advantage, as is fluency in how each organisation works, where it sits in the market and what it is seeking to achieve commercially. Deciding which competencies to pursue and in what order and keeping them current.

Thought leadership and public voice - Providing thought leadership on applied AI and establishing Cloudscaler's public voice through speaking, meetups, blogs and whitepapers. Building our standing in external applied AI communities and contributing to industry discussion, with material grounded in work we have delivered.

Market awareness - Tracking the AI market as it moves - model releases, tooling and emerging frameworks - and forming a clear view on what is credible, what is hype, and what Cloudscaler should adopt. Bringing that view to the Leadership Team early enough to act on it, and setting our position on what we adopt, what we monitor and what we set aside.

Internal responsibilities

These responsibilities cover the commercial, delivery and capability side of the business unit.

Commercial accountability - Carrying full commercial accountability for the business unit, which is run as its own business and measured on clear financial metrics: pipeline, revenue and gross profit. In the first six months that means a six-month revenue plan, with forecast gross profit covering the cost of the leader within six months and the team gross profit positive within two quarters. This grows into full P&L ownership as the unit scales, including team economics that stand on their own.

Reporting and investment cases - Reporting to the Leadership Team on monthly KPIs covering pipeline, utilisation and gross profit against the six-month plan, and building the investment cases that fund the unit's growth. Reporting runs from month one, including the business case for establishing a dedicated team.

Technical delivery oversight - Providing technical delivery oversight of AI customer engagements, working with our delivery teams. This is an architect's role rather than an engineer's: technical enough to hold your own with client engineers and to delegate the detail, and disciplined enough not to commit to capabilities we cannot feasibly deliver. Reviewing architecture and design decisions and acting as the decision-maker when a technical call is needed.

Building and leading the practice - Building and leading our AI practice: owning Cloudscaler's AI strategy and the roadmap to deliver it, hiring and line-managing the team as it grows, capability development, and a repeatable methodology and delivery standards that make quality consistent regardless of who is leading the engagement. Defining the capability model and establishing the practice as an internal centre of excellence for review and quality assurance as it grows.

Decomposing and delegating ownership - Breaking broad areas of activity into distinct responsibilities that can be delegated and genuinely owned, and building the team to hold them. The scope of this role is deliberately broader than one person can carry: the expectation is that the Head of Applied AI grows a team around them - including the AI enablement hires already in train - and leads through that team rather than delivering everything personally. Internal AI usage guidance, reviewing internal projects, pre-sales attendance, marketing campaigns and enablement workshops each need a named owner; an informal approach works while the unit is small but will not scale.

Accelerators and intellectual property - Building reusable AI accelerators and intellectual property that shorten and de-risk customer delivery. Registering the assets as the work matures - accelerators, frameworks and reference architectures - and working with engineering to keep them testable and current as models and tooling evolve. Treating them as Cloudscaler intellectual property with standalone value rather than delivery tools alone.

Company-wide AI enablement - Enabling every Cloudscaler employee to work with AI, including defining our internal AI learning pathways. Setting the guidance for how AI is used in our own work and running the enablement activity that puts it into everyday use across the whole company rather than the practice alone.

Internal community of practice - Growing an internal AI community of practice, giving colleagues outside the team a route to learn and contribute. Running it as a standing forum rather than ad-hoc sessions, so that colleagues outside the practice can build AI capability alongside their own work.

Candidate profile

This is a senior role combining technical depth with commercial ownership. We expect candidates to demonstrate the following:

Technical depth in applied AI - Current, hands-on understanding of AI technologies, models and tooling, sufficient to direct development work, review architecture and design decisions, and hold credible technical conversations with client engineers and architects.

Commercial track record - Experience owning a revenue or gross profit target, building the pipeline behind it, and reporting against a plan. Comfortable being measured on financial outcomes rather than activity.

Consulting and client credibility - A strong communicator who can advise at C-suite level and at engineering level, and whom clients want in the room on their most significant decisions.

Practice or capability building - Experience building a team or capability from a small base: hiring, setting delivery standards, and creating repeatable methodology rather than relying on individual heroics.

Partner ecosystem experience - Familiarity with the AWS and Anthropic ecosystems, or a comparable hyperscaler and model-vendor landscape, including how partner competencies and joint go-to-market activity work in practice.

External profile - A track record of public contribution on applied AI, or the clear appetite and ability to build one.

Leadership and delegation - Experience leading and line-managing a technical team, including setting direction, delegating genuine ownership and developing people. Comfortable achieving outcomes through a team rather than personally delivering the work.

Judgement and prioritisation - The ability to decide where to concentrate a small team's effort, and the discipline to stop work that is not producing.

Benefits

  • Discretionary bonus

  • Discretionary security clearance bonus for those holding certain clearance

  • Periodic offer of share options schemes

  • 25 days’ annual leave

  • 5 additional days per year towards training, certifications, or charity work

  • Option to buy additional annual leave up to 5 days per year

  • Public holidays opt-out scheme, the option to work on public holidays creating the flexibility to enjoy your time off when it suits you

  • Certifications and training expensed

  • Life Assurance

  • Long Term Disability cover

  • Employee Assist Programme for employee advice and support (including legal and counselling helpline)

  • Health, Mental Health, Wellbeing, Financial and Legal support

  • 24/7 GP access

  • Pension auto-enrolment and contribution

  • Employee referral scheme

  • Client referral scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Travel expenses policy

 

Interview Process

  1. Chat with Talent Team

  2. Remote interview with Hiring Manager

  3. Final in-person with Leadership Team

title: Head of CS - Nachunternehmer (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über Cosuno

Die Baubranche ist eine 14-Billionen-Euro-Industrie, die noch immer auf E-Mails, Excel-Tabellen und eingescannten PDFs läuft. Cosuno ersetzt das durch KI. Generalunternehmer schreiben ihre Projekte auf unserer Plattform an mehr als 250.000 Nachunternehmer aus, und unsere agentische KI findet die passenden Firmen, erkennt Auffälligkeiten in Angeboten und vergleicht jeden Preis mit 6,5 Millionen Datenpunkten aus über 136 Milliarden Euro verarbeitetem Angebotsvolumen. Jede Ausschreibung macht die KI klüger. Die Ergebnisse sind messbar: Generalunternehmer senken ihre Kosten um rund 6 %, Nachunternehmer gewinnen 22 % mehr Volumen, und jeder neue Generalunternehmer-Kunde hat sich in diesem Jahr für unser KI-Produkt entschieden. 2019 in Berlin gegründet und von Cherry Ventures und Spark Capital mit über 40 Millionen Euro finanziert, skalieren wir mit diesem Kapital jetzt Sales, Customer Success und Marketing. Und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

Die Rolle

Du übernimmst das SC-Customer-Success-Team und verantwortest den Churn im Nachunternehmer-Segment vollständig. Nicht als Sponsor, sondern als Owner: Aktivierungslogik, Winback-Playbook, Durchsatz je Person, Forecast. Du entscheidest, was gemessen wird, was im Playbook steht und wann es sich ändert.

Wir führen Customer Success wie Vertrieb. Du bist dafür verantwortlich, dass dieses System läuft, und du bist selbst Teil davon: Die härtesten Kündigungen und Eskalationen fährst du persönlich.

Woran wir dich nach 12 Monaten messen

  • Churn im Nachunternehmer-Segment liegt unter 20 %. Heute sind es 28 %. Das ist die eine Zahl, an der sich alles andere ausrichtet.

  • Die Winback-Quote deines Teams liegt bei mindestens 50 % der bearbeiteten Kündigungen.

  • 90 % der onboardeten Kunden sind nach 30 Tagen aktiv – und das bleibt so, während du gemeinsam mit Product die Selbstaktivierung im Produkt ausbaust.

  • Winback- und Onboarding-Playbook gehören dir: Sie laufen, werden wöchentlich gemessen und du änderst sie, wenn die Zahlen es sagen. Der wöchentliche Forecast läuft ab deinem ersten Monat.

  • Die harten Cases und Eskalationen hast du selbst geführt – und wenn das Team unter Wasser ist, mehr.

  • Product und Sales bekommen von dir strukturiert, was Kunden sagen: Kündigungsgründe, Aktivierungshürden, falsche Erwartungen aus dem Closing.

Wer bei Cosuno erfolgreich ist

  • Ownership. Du sprichst über eigene Fehler, bevor jemand fragt, und darüber, was du daraus geändert hast.

  • Speed. Du löst Probleme pragmatisch und heute, nicht perfekt und nächstes Quartal.

  • Drive. Du hast Beispiele parat, wo du Prozesse gebaut oder Probleme gelöst hast, ohne dass dich jemand darum gebeten hat.

  • Low Ego. Du redest über Team-Erfolge und gibst Credit weiter – und hast trotzdem eigene Zahlen, die du nennen kannst.

Diese Rolle ist für dich, wenn

  • du ein Team mit eigener Zahl geführt hast und weißt, wie es sich anfühlt, wenn eine Person drei Wochen unter Ziel liegt – und was du dann tust.

  • du selbst Kündigungen gedreht hast, ohne den Preis zu verschenken, und das auch noch einmal tun willst.

  • du in Cases pro Woche denkst, nicht in zwanzig Accounts, die du betreust.

  • du am Vormittag ein Playbook schreibst und am Nachmittag den Kundencall führst

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn

  • du Customer Success als Beziehungspflege verstehst und Verkaufen jemand anderem überlässt.

  • du als Head keine Kundencalls mehr machen willst.

  • du Prozesse baust, aber nie selbst gegen eine Quote gearbeitet hast.

  • du aus der Strategieberatung kommst und noch nie ein operatives SaaS-Team geführt hast.


Harte Anforderungen

  • 3–5 Jahre B2B SaaS in Customer Success, Retention, Renewals oder Account Management, davon mindestens 2 Jahre Führung eines quotentragenden Teams.

  • Eigener, belegbarer Winback- oder Renewal-Track-Record.

  • Erfahrung im SMB- oder High-Volume-Geschäft.

  • Sicher in Salesforce (oder vergleichbarem CRM) und einem BI-Tool, bei uns Looker.

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (C2), Englisch fließend. Unsere Kunden sind deutsche Handwerksbetriebe.

  • Berlin oder Bereitschaft zu mindestens zwei Bürotagen pro Woche.


Vergütung

120.000 € OTE pro Jahr (Zielgehalt bei 100 % Zielerreichung), bestehend aus einem Fixgehalt und einer variablen Komponente, die sich nach deiner Zielerreichung richtet.


Was wir bieten

  • Verantwortung: Du ownst Churn im wichtigsten Revenue-Stream des Unternehmens, mit direktem Draht zu Gründern und Geschäftsführung.

  • Vertrag: Unbefristet, moderne Ausstattung.

  • Arbeitsort: Berlin-Kreuzberg oder hybrid, du wählst.

  • Entwicklung: Regelmäßige 1:1s, Entwicklungsgespräche, offene Feedbackkultur.

  • Team: Firmen- und Teamevents, online und offline.

title: Head of Customer Success
descriptionHtml:
About Rivia

Rivia is a data engine for clinical trial intelligence. It provides data infrastructure and AI-driven workflows for clinical trial teams, enabling biotechs to run studies more efficiently and to demonstrate which patients derive the greatest benefit from new therapies. Biopharma companies are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is frequently slowed by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia delivers a real-time, integrated view across clinical trial data, improving both trial execution and the evaluation of new treatments.

 

Our goal is for Rivia to become the new standard infrastructure for modern drug development, bringing new therapies to market more successfully at a fraction of the cost.

 

We seek highly self-motivated, motivated and talented professionals to contribute to our growing startup.

 

About the role

We are looking for a hands-on Head of Customer Success to lead and scale how Rivia delivers value to customers. As our first dedicated Customer Success leader, you will oversee the post-sales journey, from onboarding and technical implementation through adoption, retention, and long-term account growth.

You will lead Customer Engagement and Solutions Engineering, build a repeatable operating model, and stay close to strategic biotech and pharmaceutical customers. You will combine scientific and technical credibility with strong people leadership, commercial judgment, and a builder’s mindset.

Ownership and Commercial Collaboration

Customer Success owns the post-sales customer relationship, implementation, adoption, measurable value realization, customer health, retention strategy, and renewal readiness. The They will be accountable for customer outcomes and for proactively identifying and developing expansion opportunities.

Sales owns the commercial pipeline and execution of renewal and upsell transactions, including commercial negotiations and closing. The Head of Customer Success partners closely with Sales to shape account strategies, quantify customer value, identify and qualify opportunities, manage renewal risks, and support successful commercial outcomes.

What excites you

  • Building something from the ground up. You're excited by the opportunity to shape and scale a Customer Success function, creating the structure, processes, and standards that will support Rivia's next stage of growth.

  • Making a real impact on drug development. You're motivated by working at the intersection of life sciences and technology, helping biotech companies make better decisions and accelerate clinical development.

  • Being close to customers. You enjoy understanding complex scientific and technical challenges, building trusted relationships, and translating customer needs into meaningful outcomes.

  • Combining leadership with hands-on execution. You love developing high-performing teams but are equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves, solving difficult problems, and taking ownership of strategic accounts.

  • Driving measurable business impact. You're energized by improving customer retention, demonstrating value, and identifying opportunities to grow customer relationships in close partnership with Sales.

  • Thriving in a fast-paced environment. You enjoy autonomy, ambitious goals, and the opportunity to influence decisions directly, without waiting for someone else to tell you what to do.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and coach the Customer Engagement and Solutions Engineering teams, setting clear standards for performance, development, capacity planning, and hiring.

  • Build and scale the end-to-end post-sales experience, including onboarding, implementation, technical delivery, success plans, executive business reviews, escalation management, and value realization.

  • Own customer health, adoption, retention strategy, and renewal readiness; partner with Sales on renewal and expansion planning and execution.

  • Oversee complex implementations, integration quality, delivery timelines, and smooth handoffs from Sales.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior scientific, technical, and business stakeholders at biotech and pharma customers.

  • Translate platform usage into measurable outcomes, including time saved, costs avoided, and operational improvements.

  • Define and monitor customer success metrics, including adoption, time to value, GRR, NRR, renewal performance, and expansion opportunities.

  • Resolve critical customer escalations and translate recurring feedback into priorities for Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales.

  • Introduce scalable account segmentation, coverage models, reporting, and operating rhythms without unnecessary bureaucracy.

What excites us:

  • Experience leading and developing customer-facing teams in a B2B technology environment, while remaining personally close to customers.

  • A background in life sciences, biomedical engineering, biotechnology, pharmaceutical development, or a closely related scientific field.

  • Experience with biotech, pharma, clinical development, scientific software, or other complex life-sciences technology customers.

  • Evidence of driving customer retention, renewals, adoption, and account expansion through cross-functional collaboration.

  • Strong understanding of SaaS economics and customer success metrics, including GRR, NRR, customer health, and renewal rates.

  • Ability to navigate technical implementations, manage executive escalations, and influence senior stakeholders.

  • A structured, hands-on leadership style, commercial judgment, direct communication, and urgency in a fast-moving environment.

What Makes You Stand Out

  • Experience building a Customer Success function at an early-stage or Series A company.

  • Deep familiarity with clinical trials, clinical data, or pharmaceutical R&D workflows.

  • Experience supporting strategic expansion in enterprise biotech or pharmaceutical accounts.

  • A track record of measurable improvements in retention, adoption, and customer outcomes.

Our Values

At Rivia, we are committed to excellence, continuous learning, and the success of both our customers and our team.

  • In it to Win it: Approach challenges with determination, resilience, and drive.

  • Embrace change: See change as an opportunity to improve.

  • Why not?: Challenge assumptions and stay curious.

  • Find the gap: Proactively identify and solve problems.

  • Collective accountability: Own outcomes together and support one another.

  • Value add solutions: Deliver meaningful, impactful results.
