title: Product Manager - Juno
descriptionHtml:
At Joko, our mission is to we help consumers save time and money when shopping online or in-store.

Founded in Paris, Joko is a tech company and certified B Corp with over 120 talents across Paris, Barcelona, and New York (and beyond). More than 7 million users already save money every day at 10,000+ merchants with Joko.

From cashback and automatic coupons to price alerts, we've kept expanding our products to make shopping smarter. Today, Joko is an AI shopping app: with Juno, our shopping assistant, users can find the right product at the best price in only a few seconds, with recommendations that get sharper the more they use it.

Having reached profitability in our core market, we’re now scaling globally, with a strong focus on the US.

It’s still day 1, come build the future of shopping with us!

📱 Our Product Team

Led by Fabien, our VP Product, Joko's Product team groups the passionate individuals behind our users' delight! From brainstorming to development to launch, the Product team's main mission is to turn ideas into reality by working hand-in-hand with the Engineering, Design, and Business teams.

Joko is organized into four product tribes, each owning a key dimension of the company's value:

  • Business lines owns the current core value proposition, covering online shopping, in-store experiences, and gift cards, each run as a dedicated team.

  • Scale focuses on growing and amplifying this value through growth, international expansion, and shared core user experiences across the app.

  • Juno builds the next value proposition: an AI shopping assistant that finds the right product at the best price in seconds, backed by a universal catalog of what merchants actually sell.

  • AI Platform helps Joko become a state-of-the-art AI company from the inside, owning the internal agent infrastructure, automation layer, internal tools, infrastructure, compliance, security and operational scalability.

🤖 The Engine task force

Juno is Joko's most ambitious bet: becoming the front door to shopping. An AI assistant that understands what someone is genuinely looking for, searches thousands of merchants at once, and gets them to the right decision in seconds rather than hours — the reflex people reach for before they buy anything.

The Juno tribe is split into two task forces. Engine owns the assistant itself: the conversational experience users interact with, and the product logic that turns an intent into the right recommendation. Catalog owns the universal product catalog that powers it.

Engine is where Juno meets the user. It owns the conversation itself: how someone expresses a vague intent, how the assistant narrows it down, and how a recommendation is presented so that it is actually trusted. Nobody has settled what a great shopping conversation looks like, so there are no patterns to borrow and the answers have to be found by building and testing.

The task force is a small, autonomous team: a Product Manager who owns it, a Product Designer, and software engineers. This role is its first Product Manager, so the scope, the standards, and the way the team works are yours to define.

🎯 What you will do

As Product Manager for the Engine task force, you own it. That means the end-to-end user experience of Juno, from the conversational interface on mobile and web to the product logic behind the recommendations. You will report to Yosr, who leads the Juno tribe, and work day to day with a Product Designer, software engineers, and the Catalog task force.

  • Conversational product design: There is no market standard for what a great shopping conversation looks like. You will define it. That means testing a lot, iterating fast, and inventing interaction patterns for a surface that has none yet.

  • Designing with AI's limits in mind: A model-backed flow behaves differently from a deterministic one. You will design for hallucinations, unexpected outputs, and edge cases: what the fallback is, what the model gets fed, what the user sees when it goes wrong. This is a large part of the craft in this role.

  • Discovery, user testing & iteration: You will run user tests continuously, read real conversations, spot where the experience breaks, and turn that into the next iteration. You will own the rollout strategy and decide what ships to whom, when.

  • Roadmap & ownership: You will define the vision and roadmap for the assistant experience, prioritise against company priorities and technical reality, and own delivery from problem framing to launch.

  • Measurement: Evaluating an AI experience is a hard problem in itself. You will define what quality means for Juno, build the metrics that track it, and use them to drive decisions.

  • Competitive positioning: Generic assistants ship new shopping capabilities constantly. You will define what makes a specialised shopping assistant win.

👀 Who we're looking for

  • Experience: You have at least 2 to 3 years of experience as a Product Manager. We are flexible on seniority, but you need enough depth to bring real experience to a team that is being built.

  • AI product experience: You have shipped user-facing features powered by AI, on a product with a meaningful user base. You know what it takes to put a model in front of real users and keep the experience good.

  • UX & UI judgment: You have strong instincts on user experience and interface, and you have wrestled with the specific difficulty of designing an AI feature. This role is deeply user-facing, and this criterion carries the most weight.

  • Data fluency: You are comfortable defining metrics, instrumenting them, and evaluating outcomes with numbers. Every decision on this team is backed by data.

  • AI fluency: You are hands-on and genuinely curious about AI tools and how models behave. Juno is built on AI, so you will be in the product every day.

  • ML knowledge: A strong bonus. The engineers bring that depth already, so we weigh UX judgment on AI features more heavily than model internals.

  • 0-to-1 appetite: You want to build something that does not exist yet. Blank pages energise you.

  • Location: Based in France or Spain.

  • Languages: Fluent in English, both written and spoken. French is a plus, but it is optional.

  • Mindset: You have an entrepreneurial mindset, you like challenges, you welcome feedback and you love constantly learning and getting better.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

  • 💸 Top-market compensation

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

  • 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

  • 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

  • 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

  • …and much more, check the full list here!

🤝 Our hiring process

  1. Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

  2. Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

  3. Step 2 – Role-specific assessments

    • For non-engineering roles: A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

    • For engineering roles: A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

  4. Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

  5. References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

☕ You may also be invited for coffee with team members to get a feel for our culture.

Compensation: €64K – €104K • Offers Equity

title: Product Marketing & Growth Intern (H/F)
descriptionHtml:
About Pysae

Pysae is a French SaaS company building real-time fleet supervision (AVM / SAEIV) and workforce management software for public transport operators. Bus networks, coach operators and transport authorities in France and across Europe rely on our platform every day to run their services, inform passengers and manage their drivers. We are a team of around 40 people based in Rennes, Paris and Italy, and we are expanding fast internationally.

Pysae has grown from a set of products into a full platform. We now need someone to help tell that story, put it in front of the right people, and turn it into growth.

The internship

Reporting to our Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), you will work on product marketing and growth: generating demand through the product itself and by showcasing the value of the Pysae platform. You will be given real responsibilities from day one, not side tasks.

This is an international role. You will work on France, Italy and our new markets across Europe and beyond, with sales teams and customers in several countries and languages.

This is not a classic marketing internship. Our market (public transport operators and authorities) has long been sold to in the same way: tenders, trade shows and long sales cycles. We want to break that pattern. Your mission is to help us invent, test and deploy new ways of selling and growing, using the product, content, data and AI as levers. You will have a blank page, direct access to the CRO and the founders, and the freedom to try things that have never been done in our industry.

It is a very exciting internship, and a demanding one: you will need to come up with ideas, prove quickly whether they work, drop what doesn't and scale what does.

Your missions

Invent new sales & growth methods

  • Imagine new ways to reach, engage and convert transport operators and authorities, beyond the traditional tender-driven playbook

  • Design and run fast experiments (new channels, formats, offers, outreach sequences, product-led motions), measure the results and turn the winners into repeatable playbooks for the sales team

  • Bring fresh ideas from other industries and from the latest AI and growth practices, and adapt them to our market

Product marketing & positioning

  • Help sharpen the positioning and messaging of the Pysae platform and its modules for each segment (urban networks, interurban and school transport, on-demand transport, rail) and each country

  • Turn product releases into launches: release notes, feature pages, demo videos, customer-facing announcements

  • Build sales enablement material with the sales team, in French and English: pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, battlecards, ROI arguments

International growth

  • Create and run campaigns (LinkedIn, email, webinars, international trade shows, content) that generate qualified pipeline for the sales team

  • Produce creative content that showcases the platform and our customers: case studies, articles, videos, social posts

  • Track and report on what works (traffic, leads, conversion, adoption) and double down on it

AI & automation

  • Use AI tools intensively to create and translate content, personalise outreach, analyse data and run campaigns at scale

  • Automate as many marketing and sales workflows as possible (CRM, emailing, reporting, content production), and document them so they keep running after your internship

Practical details

title: Product & Yield Engineer (Data-focused)
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

We are looking for an Engineer to play a key role in the development and manufacture of Fractile's silicon products, with a particular focus on product, yield and manufacturing data analysis. Working across New Product Introduction (NPI), Yield Engineering and Product Quality, you will analyse large and complex semiconductor datasets to identify trends, isolate sources of variation, improve yield and reliability, and provide clear technical insight to engineering teams and manufacturing partners. This is a highly hands-on individual contributor role for someone who enjoys working directly with data, investigating complex technical problems and turning analysis into actionable engineering conclusions.

Skills and Experience

  • Demonstrable experience within the semiconductor industry in Product Engineering, Test Engineering, Yield Engineering, Data Analytics or Quality Engineering, ideally spanning NPI through to high-volume production

  • Strong experience analysing semiconductor manufacturing and test data to identify trends, correlations, excursions, yield loss mechanisms and opportunities for improvement

  • Solid experience in as many of the following areas as possible:

    • Wafer fab: analysis of Process Integration, Yield Enhancement, D0 Control, defect reduction and process variation data

    • IC Assembly: Assembly Process or Package Design, 3D IC and wafer stacking, Assembly Quality Control, BOM optimisation and Yield Engineering

    • Fabless Semiconductor: IC Product Qualification, reliability and failure analysis, RMA investigation and production monitoring

  • Strong knowledge of WAT, WS/CP and FT datasets, including correlation across manufacturing and test stages

  • Excellent data mining, statistical analysis and root-cause investigation skills, with the ability to turn complex datasets into clear engineering conclusions

  • Experience identifying yield signatures, parameter distributions, outliers, spatial patterns, lot-to-lot variation and systematic versus random failure mechanisms

  • Extensive hands-on use of semiconductor industry data analysis tools and software such as yieldHUB, Spotfire, JMP or equivalent

  • Ability to create scripts, automated analyses, dashboards and repeatable analytical workflows for standard engineering investigations and reporting

  • Experience applying statistical methods to semiconductor manufacturing data, including SPC, Cp/Cpk, distributions, correlation analysis, hypothesis testing and trend analysis

  • Ability to combine data from multiple sources and manufacturing stages to investigate complex product and process issues

  • Familiarity with FMEA-derived semiconductor qualification plans and relevant standards such as JEDEC

  • Understanding of semiconductor failure analysis methods and the ability to use analytical data to guide selection of destructive and non-destructive investigation techniques

  • Strong ability to communicate analytical findings through concise visualisations, reports and technical presentations

  • Comfortable working independently on ambiguous technical problems and driving investigations from initial data exploration through to a supported conclusion

  • Good communication skills and a collaborative, team-player attitude

  • Self-starter, flexible and able to manage multiple analyses and investigations in parallel

  • Willing and able to travel worldwide when needed

Desirable

  • Experience building automated semiconductor yield-monitoring, reporting or anomaly-detection workflows

  • Experience working with large semiconductor datasets using SQL, Python or similar data-analysis tools

title: Production Engineer, Network
descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Production Engineering Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Turn every network fault from a mystery into a closed ticket. Link diagnostics across router to router and NIC to router paths, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows what's broken and why, because at 10s of GW scale debugging has to be systematic, not artisanal.

  • Build the network repair pipeline that runs itself. Automated fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver lifecycle tracking, and return to service, across DC fabric, edge, and host to network layers, because a new site comes online every six months and manual repair doesn't keep up.

  • Build the network monitoring platform for a fleet that never stops growing. Alerting lifecycle and health dashboards for infrastructure spanning multiple hyperscale sites today and 10s of GW next year. It doesn't exist yet. We're building it.

Role Scope

  • Carry the on-call pager for the network fleet and run repair end to end: diagnose the fault, execute the fix or drive the RMA, and return the link to service across DC fabric, edge, and host to network layers.

  • Write Python and Go tooling that replaces manual diagnosis, including link tests, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows what's broken and why, so faults resolve in minutes, not hours.

  • Automate the repair pipeline from fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver and optics tracking, and return to service, so a failure at any site follows the same path without manual handoffs.

  • Maintain the realtime monitoring and alerting that gives every on-call engineer a true picture of network health across all sites, and keep it accurate as new sites and hardware roll in.

  • Validate new sites and hardware into production by running the qualification tests that confirm a network is healthy before it carries traffic.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've carried a pager for a production network and can walk into an outage, find the fault, fix it or drive the RMA, and write the postmortem without someone walking you through it.

  • You've written Python or Go scripts that replaced a manual, repetitive network task, from link diagnostics to config pushes to fleet-wide command execution.

  • You understand how a transceiver fault, a misconfigured route, and a power event each show up differently in the data, and you can tell them apart from the signals alone.

  • You've worked hands-on with link diagnostics, optics, and network monitoring protocols such as gNMI, gRPC, NETCONF, and SONiC, and you're comfortable at the CLI on switches and routers across a fleet.

  • You treat toil as a bug. If a repair step means SSHing into ten boxes by hand, you script it once and never do it by hand again.

  • You reach real competence in an unfamiliar part of the stack fast, and you document what you learn so the next on-call engineer doesn't start from zero.

  • Bonus: RMA and repair lifecycle automation. Large-scale datacenter fabric (BGP, ECMP, spine-leaf). Out-of-band network management. Fluency with AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor to move faster on scripts and tooling.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

descriptionHtml:
About WPP Production

We are WPP Production - the unified global production company that brings together all of WPP's content producers, studios and craft experts into one connected organisation. We combine world-class human craft with next generation technology to originate, design, and deliver multi-channel content systems at scale. WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com.

A Hybrid working model

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

The role

We’re looking for a Programme Director to lead the end-to-end delivery of a complex, high-profile programme at the intersection of creative production, AI and emerging technology.

You will translate strategic objectives into an integrated delivery plan, bring multiple workstreams together and ensure the programme delivers against its commitments. You’ll take ownership of programme governance, dependencies, risks and decisions, providing the clarity and control needed to navigate complexity and maintain momentum.

Working across senior leadership, technology partners, clients and multidisciplinary delivery teams, you’ll connect the bigger picture with the detail of execution, ensuring everyone is aligned on what needs to happen, when and why.

What you’ll do

Lead the programme

  • Own the integrated programme plan, translating objectives into clear workstreams, milestones, deliverables and success measures.
  • Establish effective governance, clear accountability and a consistent approach to programme reporting and decision-making.
  • Maintain oversight of the critical path, dependencies and delivery commitments, ensuring activity across workstreams comes together to achieve the overall programme objectives.
  • Provide a clear view of programme health, progress and emerging issues, giving leadership the information needed to make timely, informed decisions.

Drive delivery

  • Lead delivery across multiple workstreams, aligning teams on priorities, milestones and interdependencies.

Align clients and stakeholders

  • Lead programme reviews and executive reporting, communicating progress, risks, decisions and required actions with clarity.
  • Act as the central point of coordination for programme delivery, connecting stakeholders and ensuring commitments translate into action.

Deliver measurable outcomes

  • Maintain oversight of performance against programme objectives, milestones, budgets and agreed commercial commitments, working with the relevant commercial and finance leads.
  • Define and track success measures that demonstrate client adoption, business impact and value delivered.
  • Identify emerging delivery or commercial risks, making their implications visible and driving appropriate action.
  • Use performance data and programme insight to inform decisions, address underperformance and improve outcomes throughout the programme lifecycle.

What you’ll bring

  • Significant experience leading complex programmes involving multiple workstreams, interdependent deliverables and senior stakeholders.
  • A proven track record of translating strategic objectives into executable plans and delivering against challenging commitments.
  • Strong programme management expertise across integrated planning, governance, critical path management, risk, dependencies and change control.
  • The judgement to anticipate problems, navigate ambiguity and make effective decisions when priorities or delivery conditions change.
  • The confidence to challenge constructively, influence senior stakeholders and hold teams accountable across matrixed organisations.
  • Strong commercial awareness, including an understanding of budgets, forecasts and performance against agreed commitments.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear decisions, recommendations and executive-level reporting.
  • A proactive, collaborative approach, combining attention to detail with a clear focus on overall programme objectives.

Experience in creative production, digital transformation, AI-enabled programmes or technology partnerships would be advantageous.

What success looks like

  • A clear, integrated programme plan that connects workstreams, milestones, dependencies and outcomes.
  • Predictable, well-controlled delivery, with risks anticipated, blockers resolved and commitments actively managed.
  • Clear accountability across workstreams and strong alignment between clients, partners and delivery teams.

descriptionHtml:
About the role

Octopus is building a new business line delivering low-cost, reliable, clean energy and faster speed-to-power for data centres and large industrials. We're looking for a Project Electrical Engineer to be the electrical owner on first-of-a-kind power projects - private wire, behind-the-meter generation and storage, MV and HV grid connections.

This is a technical role with a unique expanded scope to broader infrastructure project management. Early on you are the project manager: you hold the programme, the development budget and the external parties, from concept design through connection offer to design freeze and financial close. From there you stay on as the electrical owner through construction, commissioning and energisation, with a delivery team around you.


What you'll do
  • Own the programme and the development budget. Schedule from early concept to design freeze - siting, connection application, planning, consents, procurement, long-lead items - worked back from the customer's energisation date. Appoint and manage consultants, ICPs and study providers. Surface risk early and clearly communicate them to the stakeholders.
  • Own the electrical concept through to sign-off. Single-line diagrams, general arrangements, switchgear and plant layouts, cable routes, metering and comms architecture. Direct and interrogate the studies (load flow, short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, earthing, power quality). Chair design reviews and stage gates, and take options to the Project Lead and customer with a recommendation.
  • Lead the grid interface. DNO, TO and NESO - applications and offers, technical requirements, securities and milestones, contestable and non-contestable scope, ICP/IDNO coordination, MPAN registration.
  • Budget ownership through completion. Credible capex inputs for the project model across plant, substation, civils and enabling works, with value engineering and optioneering. Then FAT/SAT witnessing, commissioning plans and sequences of operation, energisation and handover.
  • Take on what you haven't done before. First-of-a-kind means no precedent, no standard design and no colleague who's done it. Get to a working understanding of an unfamiliar technology or scope fast, and deliver it.

    • What you'll have
  • Master’s degree, or equivalent, in electrical or power systems engineering. CEng welcome, not essential.
  • 5+ years delivering energy or infrastructure projects, with a strong grounding in MV and HV systems.
  • Real infrastructure experience - substations, networks, industrial plant, data centres, utilities, water or transport. We care that you've dealt with ground conditions, easements, consents, tie-ins to live assets and construction sequencing. This is not a grid-only role.
  • You've personally held a programme and a budget on a development or pre-construction project.

  • Able to coordinate a multi-discipline design where you're not the expert in every discipline - and to spot a weak answer from a civil or mechanical engineer.

title: Project Manager
descriptionHtml:
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

About the Role

As a Project Manager at Sona, you'll own a portfolio of enterprise implementations end to end, working alongside a Solutions Architect on each project. Assignments are based on capacity and fit rather than a fixed team, so you'll work across sectors, hospitality, retail and social care.

You'll run implementations of Sona's products (HR, Scheduling, Payroll, LMS & ATS) end to end, ensuring delivery meets our scope commitments, budgets and timelines, all while providing an exceptional experience for our customers. You'll partner closely with senior stakeholders from our customers and internally across our Commercial, Product and Customer teams. We're a growing business, so you'll also need to thrive in a fast-evolving environment and be a strong advocate for clarity and communication.


Responsibilities

  • Lead and deliver projects on time, within scope and budget, maintaining the highest quality standards.

  • Manage project risks, dependencies and scope, communicating mitigations and changes clearly to all stakeholders.

  • Act as the primary customer advocate, building strong relationships and managing expectations throughout delivery.

  • Coordinate internal teams, vendors and customers to ensure successful outcomes and efficient resource deployment.

  • Produce clear, consistent documentation and status reports, escalating risks where required.

  • Support our Land and Expand approach by driving strong customer partnerships and early value realisation.

  • Continuously improve project processes and tools to enhance delivery speed, quality and customer satisfaction.

Requirements

  • Proven success delivering enterprise software implementation projects on time, within budget and scope.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including working with C-level executives.

  • Strong leadership and collaboration skills, able to influence without direct authority.

  • Strategic thinker with strong risk management, planning and prioritisation capabilities.

  • Calm, organised and results-driven under pressure, with excellent time management.

  • Confident in presenting, reporting and managing multiple complex projects simultaneously.

  • Comfortable using AI in your own workflow, notes, actions, tracking, and able to explain where you'd trust it and where you wouldn't.

  • Bonus: experience with workforce management or HR software, prior use of Smartsheets, experience managing customers in a frontline or operationally complex industry.

We're a hybrid working team you can expect to work 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho), and 2+ days/week on site with customers.

title: Projectontwikkelaar woningbouw
descriptionHtml:
Wil jij bouwen aan de woningbouwopgave én aan een nieuwe ontwikkelorganisatie? Als Senior Projectontwikkelaar bij Dura Vermeer Bouw & Vastgoed werk je aan grootschalige woningbouwprojecten in Midden-Nederland. Je stapt in na tendergunning en bent verantwoordelijk voor de verdere ontwikkeling richting realisatie. In een ondernemende omgeving krijg je alle ruimte om mee te bouwen aan het team, je expertise in te zetten in de samenwerking met bouwpartners én door te groeien naar een rol met meer inhoudelijke en coachende verantwoordelijkheid.

Dit wordt jouw baan

Ondernemend, ervaren en klaar om impact te maken? Dan voel jij je thuis binnen deze nieuwe ontwikkelorganisatie van Dura Vermeer. Als Senior Projectontwikkelaar werk je aan omvangrijke woningbouwontwikkelingen en help je niet alleen projecten verder te brengen, maar ook het team en de organisatie. Je begrijpt hoe ontwikkeling en bouw elkaar versterken, neemt eigenaarschap en krijgt de ruimte om mee te denken, mee te bouwen en mee te groeien. Je bent betrokken vanaf de fase na tendergunning en schakelt intensief met de bouw om projecten succesvol richting uitvoering te brengen. Daarnaast krijg je de mogelijkheid om in de toekomst ontwikkelaars te begeleiden en bijvoorbeeld door te groeien naar een rol als Hoofd Vastgoedontwikkeling.

Wat ga je doen

Deze functie richt zich nadrukkelijk niet op de initiatieffase of acquisitiekant van gebieds- en vastgoedontwikkeling. De focus ligt op het moment waarop een tender is gewonnen en projecten daadwerkelijk gerealiseerd gaan worden. Je werkt aan (midel)grote woningbouwontwikkelingen van honderden woningen en bent de verbindende factor tussen ontwikkeling en bouw. Dat maakt deze rol ideaal voor een ervaren ontwikkelaar die energie krijgt van het realiseren van projecten, ondernemerschap toont en wil meegroeien met een ambitieuze organisatie.

· Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de ontwikkeling van woningbouwprojecten vanaf tendergunning tot aan de start van de realisatie;

· Je stuurt het ontwikkelproces aan op het gebied van kwaliteit, planning, financiën en risico's;

· Je verbindt de belangen van gemeenten, adviseurs, beleggers, corporaties, bouwteams en andere stakeholders;

· Je werkt intensief samen met collega's van Bouw om projecten optimaal uitvoerbaar en haalbaar te maken;

· Je vertaalt ambities en plannen naar concrete ontwikkelbeslissingen die bijdragen aan een succesvolle uitvoering;

· Je voert regie op vergunningstrajecten, overeenkomsten en besluitvorming;

· Je bewaakt de businesscase en stuurt op waardecreatie gedurende het gehele ontwikkelproces;

· Je draagt actief bij aan de verdere opbouw en professionalisering van de ontwikkelorganisatie;

· Je begeleidt en coacht minder ervaren projectontwikkelaars en krijgt de ruimte om op termijn een meer aansturende rol te vervullen.

Meer bij Dura Vermeer

Dura Vermeer is een onafhankelijk familiebedrijf. En dat merk je. In hoe we samenwerken, naar elkaar omkijken en bouwen met oog voor de volgende generaties. Al sinds 1855 bouwen we aan Nederland, in woningbouw, utiliteitsbouw, infrastructuur en techniek. Onze onafhankelijkheid en lange termijn visie vormen daarbij de basis.

Met een omzet van € 2,6 miljard en ruim 3.700 collega’s behoren we tot de top van de Nederlandse bouwsector. Maar uiteindelijk draait het bij ons niet om die cijfers. Het draait om mensen. Om collega’s die samen werken aan projecten waar je trots op bent iconisch én dichtbij en bijdragen aan oplossingen voor maatschappelijke vraagstukken.

Onze ambities zijn groot. En die maken we alleen waar met betrokken mensen. Daarom investeren we in goed werkgeverschap en een werkomgeving waarin jij je thuis voelt. Waar je jezelf kunt zijn, je veilig voelt en je uitspreekt. Zodat jij het beste uit jezelf haalt en samen met ons meer maakt.


Hier zit je op jouw plek

Bij Dura Vermeer Bouw en Vastgoed Utrecht staan we aan het begin van een nieuw hoofdstuk. Waar we jarenlang bekend stonden als een sterke renovatie/transformatiespecialist, zijn we sinds begin dit jaar uitgegroeid tot een volwaardige Bouw en Vastgoed organisatie. Naast renovatie en transformatie realiseren we nu ook nieuwbouwprojecten in de woning- en utiliteitsbouw én zetten we de volgende stap naar eigen gebieds- en vastgoedontwikkeling.

Dat betekent dat je terechtkomt in een organisatie die volop in beweging is. Met ruim 100 collega's binnen onze werkmaatschappij bouwen we niet alleen aan duurzame woningen, utiliteitsprojecten en leefomgevingen, maar ook aan de toekomst van onze eigen organisatie. De lijnen zijn kort, de ambities groot en de kansen om mee te bouwen aan nieuwe werkwijzen, teams en projecten liggen voor het oprapen.

Hier krijg je de ruimte om impact te maken. Niet vanaf de zijlijn, maar midden in een frisse organisatie die zich verder ontwikkelt en waarin ondernemerschap, samenwerking en eigenaarschap centraal staan. Samen bouwen we aan projecten waar we trots op zijn én aan een organisatie die klaar is voor de toekomst.


Dit breng jij mee

· Minimaal 5 tot 10 jaar ervaring als projectontwikkelaar, ontwikkelmanager of vergelijkbare functie;

· Een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding;

· Ervaring met woningbouwontwikkelingen;

· Aantoonbare ervaring met projecten van substantiële omvang (200+ woningen is een pre).;

· Ruime ervaring met ontwikkeltrajecten in de SO-, VO- en DO-fases, het verkrijgen van omgevingsvergunningen en verkooptrajecten;

· Inzicht in bouwtechnische uitgangspunten om adviseurs aan te sturen en het plan verder uit te werken;

· Ervaring binnen een ontwikkelaar, ontwikkelende bouwer of vastgoedorganisatie.

Je bent een ontwikkelaar die vooral energie krijgt van de projecten na tendergunning verder te brengen richting realisatie. Je begrijpt de dynamiek van de bouw en weet hoe je samen met alle betrokken partijen woningbouwprojecten succesvol kunt ontwikkelen én realiseren.

Dit bieden wij jou

  • Het salaris voor deze functie ligt bij een medior profiel tussen € 5.639,- en € 7.049,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur) en bij een senior profiel tussen € 6.512,- en € 9.512,- (op basis van 40 uur), exclusief 8% vakantiegeld. Het exacte salaris is afhankelijk van jouw kennis, niveau en werkervaring.

title: Python Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

This role sits within our mortgage engineering team. You’ll work across the backend stack, owning features end to end: from shaping product and technical requirements through implementation, launch, and iteration.

What makes someone successful in this role

You don’t just “take tickets.” You think like a product builder. You’re hungry to learn, quick to take ownership, and motivated by the chance to grow fast. You notice when a system could be simpler, when an API could be clearer, or when a technical decision needs more care.

You’re comfortable stepping into ambiguity, asking good questions, making decisions, and pushing work over the finish line.

title: QA Engineer - Quantum Computing (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Quantum computing is a new computing paradigm rapidly approaching commercial viability. Our unique approach combines laser-cooled trapped ions with microwave control and tailored magnetic fields. Our next-generation computing machines under development will be able to find solutions to problems that are out of reach today, thus enabling new innovative products and services for a brighter future.

We are looking for a QA Engineer (m/f/d) to join us in Hamburg or Siegen.

You will take ownership of quality across our software platform, from compilation services and the public API to the interfaces used by our operators and customers.

This is a build-from-scratch role: there is no ready-made test suite waiting for you, and no expensive tool that does the thinking for you. You define what good testing looks like here, and then you build it.

You are as comfortable writing a test strategy on a blank page as you are writing the automation that implements it in code.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the testing approach for our platform end-to-end: define what to test, at which level, and why

  • Write test concepts from scratch — risk-based, covering unit, integration, system, and end-to-end levels, and turn them into running, maintained automation

  • Build and own our test automation frameworks in code, integrated directly into our CI/CD pipelines, using your defined tooling

  • Do the exploratory and manual testing that automation can't cover, and know where that line sits

  • Establish quality gates, coverage expectations, and clear bug-reporting practices the whole team can work with

  • Work closely with backend, platform, and hardware teams to test at the boundaries where software meets the machine

  • Raise the testing literacy of the engineering team, so quality is a shared habit rather than a gate at the end


Required Skills:

  • 3+ years in software quality assurance, with real ownership of test strategy, not only executing predefined test scripts

  • Ability to design a test concept for an unfamiliar system: choosing the right test levels, techniques, and priorities from first principles

  • Confident programming ability (Python preferred), enough to build and maintain automation yourself rather than depend on record-and-playback tools

  • Hands-on experience with open-source testing frameworks (e.g. pytest, Playwright, Selenium) and integrating tests into CI/CD

  • Solid grounding in testing fundamentals: test design techniques, the test pyramid, API testing, and when to automate versus test manually

  • A generalist, tool-agnostic mindset, you pick the right approach for the problem, not the one tool you already know

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with experimental physicists and engineers

  • Strong adaptability and a quick learning mindset

  • Good proficiency in English (written and spoken)

Nice to have (Bonus)

  • Experience setting up a QA function or test strategy in an early-stage or greenfield environment

  • Testing distributed systems, APIs, or cloud-native services

  • Performance, load, or security testing experience

  • Exposure to hardware-in-the-loop or lab/control-software testing

  • ISTQB certification, or an equivalent grounding in test theory you actually apply

  • Prior exposure to quantum computing or other deep-tech domains


What you can expect from eleQtron:

  • Competitive salary: We value our team members and therefore provide remuneration that reflects this, additionally rewarding achievements

  • Flexible working hours: We offer personal freedom through a variety of flexible work schedules

  • Team spirit: In our international and diverse team, and with our regular team events, having fun at work is simply part of the culture

  • Further development: We want to grow together, and so we offer our team members needs-based, individualised further training as well as plenty of room for personal development

  • Bike Leasing: Stay Mobile and Sustainable with Our Company Bike Leasing Program

  • Moving Benefits: A warm welcome! We are happy to support employees who move for us with a bonus

  • At the forefront: Work at the forefront of technology, where academic research meets commercial applications

  • Modern workplace: We have a high-quality infrastructure with laboratory space, offices and meeting rooms

title: Recruiter (Temporary Contract)
descriptionHtml:
This is a temporary role, running from now until around February 2027. It is not a permanent position.

Location: London (next to East Croydon Station)

Hybrid: 2 days in the office - negotiable

Contract: Temporary, from now until around February 2027

Reports to: Head of Talent Acquisition (Joe Morrison)

Compensation: £30,000 to £35,000 pro rata, depending on experience

Target start: ASAP

About Us

Hozah is a tech-led, award-winning company driving change in the parking industry and reimagining urban mobility. Our mission is simple but powerful: to transform parking into a seamless, automated experience, paving the way for smarter, more sustainable cities.

With recent recognition as PayTech Company of the Year, a place among Deloitte's Top 50 Fastest Growing Tech Companies in the UK, and significant VC/PE investment, we're one of the fastest scaling companies in the country.

Role Overview

We have a busy few months ahead, with 20 to 30 hires to make before the spring. Many of them sit in our commercial and go-to-market teams, particularly junior sales, alongside site engineering and other junior roles. The difference between a good hire and a missed one is often how quickly a strong applicant gets a call.

You will be the first voice candidates hear from Hozah. Working alongside our Head of Talent Acquisition, you'll run first-round interviews at volume, by phone or video, giving every candidate a clear, compelling picture of Hozah and the role, and keeping every application moving.

After each call you'll make a recommendation, and our Head of Talent Acquisition will decide who progresses. Success in this role is simple to measure: a high, consistent volume of first interviews each week, and a high proportion of the people you recommend going on to a second interview. We want hiring managers to trust that anyone you put forward is worth their time.

You'll also support our sourcing using Metaview, and lend a hand with onboarding as new starters join.

This is a temporary contract running from now until around February 2027, and the scope can flex for the right person.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run a high, consistent volume of first-round interviews each week, particularly for commercial and go-to-market roles such as junior sales, as well as site engineering and other junior roles.

  • Represent Hozah brilliantly on every call: explain who we are, what the role involves and why it's worth joining, so strong candidates leave wanting to take the next step.

  • Write clear, structured notes after every call and make a recommendation, so our Head of Talent Acquisition can make fast progression decisions. A high proportion of the people you recommend should reach a second interview.

  • Keep the application inbox moving, booking calls promptly so no candidate waits long to hear from us, and keep the ATS accurate and up to date.

  • Source candidates directly using Metaview, so your call diary stays full when applications are thin.

  • Make sure every candidate, including those who don't progress, has a responsive and professional experience that represents Hozah well.

  • Support onboarding for new starters, such as preparing paperwork and coordinating first-day logistics, so that hires land smoothly.

Who we're looking for

  • An excellent speaker who presents confidently and persuasively, on the phone and on video. You can bring a company and a role to life in a few minutes.

  • Recruitment or resourcing experience, in-house or agency, with a track record of running high volumes of candidate calls.

  • Highly desirable: experience with commercial and go-to-market roles, such as sales, business development or account management, ideally in B2B tech or another high-growth environment.

  • Comfortable working to numbers. You know your calls per week and how many of the people you put forward reach a next stage, and you can tell us yours.

  • Highly organised, with tidy notes, a well-kept pipeline and reliable follow-up.

  • Warm, professional and at ease talking to people at every level.

  • Confident sourcing candidates directly, not just working from applications. Experience with an ATS and AI recruiting tools, ideally Metaview, would be an advantage.

  • Available to start soon and to commit to a temporary contract until around February 2027.

What We Offer

  • Hybrid working: 2 days in the office preferred, negotiable.

  • A chance to make a real difference during a key growth period for Hozah.

  • Hands-on experience with a modern recruitment tech stack.

  • A friendly, high-performing team.

  • A fully refurbished, modern office right next to East Croydon Station, with a fully stocked kitchen offering free breakfast, lunch and drinks!

title: Regional Director of Sales
descriptionHtml:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

As our Regional Director of Enterprise Sales, you act as the primary catalyst for RobCo's enterprise growth across the German market, driving large-scale industrial adoption of our Autonomous Manufacturing Platform. You will lead high-impact sales strategies, build strategic relationships with executive stakeholders in key industrial sectors, and scale our enterprise footprint from the ground up.

Your Responsibilities

  • Drive Regional Revenue: Lead and execute the German enterprise sales strategy to achieve and exceed ambitious revenue and market-penetration targets.

  • Build Executive Relationships: Target, engage, and secure long-term partnerships with C-level executives and key decision-makers across mid-market and large-scale manufacturing and industrial enterprises.

  • Champion Technical Solutions: Direct complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles by clearly communicating the strategic, financial, and technical ROI of RobCo's modular robotics and physical AI solutions.

  • Scale Enterprise Footprint: Identify and unlock new market verticals and geographic opportunities across the DACH region to continually expand the sales pipeline.

  • Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate closely with Solution Engineering and Product teams to align client requirements with product capabilities and deliver seamless rollouts.

  • Forecast with Accuracy: Maintain meticulous pipeline hygiene, actionable sales reporting, and highly accurate quarterly/annual revenue forecasts in Salesforce.

  • Represent the Brand: Position RobCo as the premier AI-driven automation provider through representation at key industry events, panel discussions, and executive roundtables.

  • Team Leadership & Enablement: Lead, mentor, and coach a high-performing team of Senior Account Executives, driving quota attainment, pipeline growth, and continuous performance management.

We're looking for someone who has:

  • Degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Industrial Management, or comparable experience.

  • Proven track record of sales leadership, with demonstrated success enabling Senior Account Executives to consistently achieve and exceed revenue targets.

  • Several years of experience in Enterprise SaaS or Hardware/Robotics Sales, specifically closing complex, high-value B2B deals within the German industrial or manufacturing sectors.

  • Proven track record of consistently exceeding enterprise sales quotas ($2M+ ARR responsibility) and managing complex, multi-month deal cycles.

  • Deep understanding of industrial automation, manufacturing workflows, or Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) models.

  • Willingness to travel up to 50-75% within Germany for client meetings, trade shows, onsite evaluations, and international team offsites.

  • Culture-aligned mindset: Strong ownership mindset, high drive for results, and a pragmatic, solution-oriented working style in a fast-paced scale-up environment.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in German and English.

Why join RobCo?

  • Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.

  • Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.

  • As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.

  • Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.

  • Wellpass membership (7,200+ studios across Germany), regular team events, and a team that takes both the work and the culture seriously.

  • Flexible working hours, a modern office, and—depending on the role—the option to work from home.

  • Regular team events—from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.

About RobCo

Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that continuously learns and improves, requiring zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. In October 2026, RobCo reached unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion US dollars, with its valuation doubling in less than nine months. With $200M raised from investors including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto, Kindred, Cherry Ventures, and the European Tech Collective, 225+ people globally, and 3.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our Bay Area Lab in San Francisco.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements.

descriptionHtml:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

The Role

We're seeking a field-tested operator to serve as the dedicated execution and enablement partner for our go-to-market teams across EMEA. As part of Revenue Operations, you'll drive the region's most critical initiatives and own the enablement that helps every customer-facing team ramp faster and perform at a higher level, bringing our global programs to life locally and building region-specific ones as Fireworks scales.

This role requires deep field experience as a former seller, Solutions Architect, or AI Field Engineer, and a working understanding of how GTM teams succeed across EMEA's markets. You'll work hand in hand with our global enablement partners, who own role-specific programs worldwide, and bring the regional point of view that makes those programs land. Your success will be measured in regional outcomes: time-to-first-deal and ramp compliance for new hires in EMEA, and ramped productivity across the region.

Please Note: This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Head of GTM Enablement. Expect ~15–20% travel across EMEA and to the US for team events and trainings.

What You'll Own

  1. Embed in EMEA leadership and drive critical regional initiatives:
    Take a standing seat in EMEA leadership forums, where you'll help shape the region's go-to-market strategy alongside your RevOps counterpart. As the regional operating model evolves, you'll drive the execution of the region's most critical initiatives, whether that's a multi-quarter transformation or a fix shipped in days.

  2. Bring global strategy and programs to life in EMEA:
    Partner with our global enablement partners to adapt each segment's strategy and programs for the region, so every EMEA team gets what works globally, tuned to how it sells locally. Then close the loop by bringing what you see in the field back to shape the next round of global programs.

  3. Design and deliver EMEA-specific enablement:
    Build and run the trainings that only the region needs, from local market and buyer dynamics to data residency and regulatory topics like GDPR and the EU AI Act. You'll set the regional enablement calendar and make sure it runs alongside, not on top of, the global one.

  4. Own ramp outcomes for new hires in EMEA:
    Pick up where global onboarding leaves off, guiding every new hire in the region through their first months in the field so they ramp just as consistently as their US peers. You'll be measured on time-to-first-deal and new hire ramp compliance across EMEA.

  5. Surface and scale EMEA best practices:
    Pinpoint what top performers across the region do differently through call reviews, field conversations, and performance data. Then scale those patterns across EMEA, and share what works with our global enablement partners so the rest of the world benefits too.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience, including significant time in a customer-facing GTM role (Account Executive, Solutions Architect, AI Field Engineer, or similar)

  • Experience enabling multiple GTM roles across EMEA markets, with a strong sense of how buying and selling differ across the region

  • Working fluency in AI/ML or developer infrastructure, and the credibility to coach both sellers and technical pre-sales teams

  • A track record of driving change across a team, with the rigor to define, track, and act on the metrics that prove it worked

  • Strong at both content development and live facilitation, from new-hire cohorts to experienced practitioners

  • Has personally built AI agents or apps, through prompting, no-code, low-code, or code, to drive seller or operational productivity (engineering degree not required)

  • Thrives in ambiguity, high ownership, and the pace of a high-growth startup

  • Based in EMEA and willing to travel ~15–20%

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience as a first- or second-line leader of a regional GTM team, or as Chief of Staff to a regional GTM leader

  • GTM experience at an AI/ML infrastructure, developer tools, or API-first and consumption-based business, with literacy in usage-based pricing models

  • Prior ownership of onboarding, ramp, or enablement programs in a matrixed global organization

  • Working proficiency in a second European language

  • Familiarity with modern enablement tooling and systems (LMS, CMS, CRM, conversation intelligence)

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

You'll lead a regional operations team, partner closely with regional and global leadership, and act as the key connector between regional execution and global capability. Regional operational leadership

Client delivery operations

Governance, cadence and decision management

Operating model execution

Resource and capacity management

Business and client enablement

  • Act as the regional operational point of coordination for enablement issues, working across Finance, HR, Technology and Implementation to unblock dependencies.

title: Release, Environments, and Change Engineer (C2)
descriptionHtml:
Release, Environments, and Change Engineer (C2)

Location: London or Bristol (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Level: C2

Team: Quality Engineering 

Contract: Permanent 

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

 

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you'll do

The Release, Environments and Change Engineer (REC Engineer) has three key areas of responsibility. You will operate Release, Environments and Change processes and procedures, and you’ll be involved in, and often lead, the identification and implementation of process improvements using AI and other tools.

You will work closely with the REC Manager and Environments Manager and operate the processes they define. These processes may rely on manual activities and controls at first, so you’ll take a leading role in replacing them with appropriate automation, and then identify mechanisms and methods to govern those automated controls.

You will collaborate with Enablement teams and engineering teams across Kaluza to make sure processes are understood, embedded and followed. You’ll be a decision maker with the authority to decline or postpone releases and changes, and you’ll handle client communication where approval is required for a change or release.

  • Operating promotion gates, making promote or block decisions between environments in line with contractual and ways-of-working agreements, and escalating high-risk calls.

  • Facilitating change approvals, release Go/No-Go meetings and release trains, preparing releases against readiness criteria and tracking per-team readiness and environment-deployed status.

  • Using AI-assisted checks to confirm quality gates are met, summarise what changed in a release, score change risk and flag incomplete or stale records, applying your own judgment to improve the reliability of the results.

  • Maintaining complete, accurate change and configuration records, keeping every change traceable across the full environment stack, and managing the change and release calendar.

  • Building and maintaining release automation, including readiness checks, artefact promotion, AI-drafted release notes and notifications, and reporting feeds.

  • Working with engineering teams in real time to roll back failed releases or apply fixes, and coordinating with incident and problem management so planned changes, hotfixes and major incidents stay in sync.

  • Communicating changes and releases internally and externally, supporting environment coordination and validation, running post-implementation reviews and retros, and giving operational input into gate definitions and the wider process.

What you’ll bring 

  • Strong organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to juggle multiple moving parts and spot incomplete records or inconsistencies.

  • Clear communication and strong facilitation skills, comfortable coordinating across teams, leading check-ins, keeping everyone aligned, driving decisions and chasing things through to completion.

  • The confidence to say no and hold the line when something isn’t ready, and to escalate when you’re unsure.

  • Comfort with Jira (or similar), including configuring boards, workflows and tickets.

  • Scripting and automation skills to build and maintain the automation around a release process (readiness checks, artefact promotion, release notes and reporting), plus familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and integrating automated testing into deployment workflows.

  • Day-to-day use of AI tooling with a critical eye, catching what it gets wrong rather than waving it through.

  • Experience building or integrating AI agents (e.g. LangChain, AutoGen, custom frameworks, MCP-based tooling), with an understanding of prompt engineering and LLM evaluation techniques such as faithfulness, relevance and LLM-as-a-judge, since traditional pass/fail assertions don’t translate well to testing AI agents.

What will set you apart

  • Any exposure to how software gets released or how environments work, even informally.

  • Light scripting or automation experience, or the appetite to learn it.

  • A calm head under time pressure.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

Our Employee Relations (ER) Partners protect fairness, consistency, and trust as we grow. You'll own our most sensitive and complex People cases, so that leads can act early.

As an ER Partner at ElevenLabs, you'll lead formal performance processes, investigations, grievances, and disciplinary matters from start to finish, working closely with Legal and outside counsel across many jurisdictions. You'll also coach leads through difficult conversations before they become formal cases, and turn what you see into playbooks, frameworks, and training that reduce risk and case volume over time.

  • Build playbooks, templates, and training that raise lead capability and cut avoidable cases.

  • Build out a self-serve ER flow for leads, so that common ER cases become scalable.

  • Partner with People Ops & Compliance teams to ensure smooth execution of terminations, local requirements, and compliance-heavy workflows.

Requirements

  • Hands-on experience leading employee relations cases, including performance management, investigations, grievances, and disciplinaries, ideally in a fast-growing company.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to handle sensitive issues with discretion, clarity, and fairness.

  • Solid working knowledge of employment law principles and comfort working alongside in-house and outside counsel.

APAC is already one of our largest regions by creators and generations; this role turns that usage into agency, brand and enterprise revenue.

You will define the APAC go-to-market, source and close the region's first lighthouse accounts yourself, open the partner routes to market that matter in Asia, and set the playbook that the next wave of APAC hires will follow. You will work closely with our Asia-based Growth team, our US-based Enterprise team, and directly with company leadership.

The ideal candidate has sold creative, marketing or AI technology across at least three APAC markets with distinct buying cultures, knows when a partner is the right route in and when direct is, and is energised by owning a region from zero.

What you'll do

Open the APAC market

  • Build and execute Higgsfield's APAC go-to-market strategy, tiered by market: active selling in Singapore, Australia and New Zealand, Korea and Hong Kong; relationship building in Southeast Asia, India and Taiwan; later investment elsewhere.

Work the ecosystem

What success looks like in year one

  • Two or more partner channels producing qualified pipeline.

Requirements

  • Partner and channel experience in APAC markets where partners are the primary route to market.

  • An existing network of senior buyers in APAC agencies, brands, media or entertainment companies.

  • Fluent English; Korean, Mandarin, Cantonese, Bahasa or Thai is a strong plus.

  • Based in, or willing to relocate to, Almaty; or based in Singapore, Australia, Hong Kong or Korea with the right to work there and able to travel across the region and to Almaty regularly.

  • Genuine enthusiasm for generative AI and hands-on fluency with Higgsfield or comparable creative AI tools.

Nice to have

title: Head of Engineering | xpate
descriptionHtml:

Company: xpate
Location: London or remote
Job Type: Full-time

About xpate

xpate has been a card acquirer since 2019. It combines acquiring and banking for B2B clients only, with €100M+ in annual revenue. About 100 people work there, around 15 of them in engineering. HQ is in London, and the team is spread across Latvia, Cyprus, Serbia and Singapore.

The business is changing. xpate is moving from direct sales to distribution through platforms and partners: embedded finance and Payfac-as-a-Service. The platform has to change with it. Tooling, data flow, processes and the release cycle all need a rebuild, and much of the workflow is still tracked by hand.

xpate also wants to become AI-native. Guardrails go around the core – the data layer and financial data – so it can’t be lost, rewritten or broken. Everything else runs through an agentic harness on top, so non-engineering teams can build their own tools by prompting agents.

What you will do

  • Lead the platform and organizational transformation from the inside, together with the current team.

  • Own the whole technical picture: infrastructure, architecture and vendors.

  • Replace the traditional PM → engineer handoff. Test the idea that engineering and product can work as one, with engineers talking directly to the business and domain experts.

  • Move code writing to LLMs with automated QA. Start where mistakes are cheap and reach the critical financial components later.

  • Hire engineers who talk to people and ask questions, not only write code. You can bring in 1–2 people who share the vision.

  • Focus on internal efficiency. The business sets the direction – the job is not to set a product or market vision of your own.

First 6 months

  • Months 1–3: bring all data flow – customer, financial and manual – into one clear perimeter.

  • Months 4–6: build the harness on top, so non-engineering teams can prompt agents, create their own tools and run their workflows.

What you need to succeed

  • You have built financial systems: ledger, reconciliation, processing, gateway, double-entry accounting. Ideally you wrote them yourself, and you know what a few cents of error cost at scale.

  • You have a strong data architecture background.

  • You can hold the full technical picture: infrastructure, architecture and vendors.

  • You are a senior engineer with proven results. Team size doesn’t matter – leading 4–5 people is fine.

  • You know code quality and review still matter, and you are ready to change how the work gets done.

What you get

  • A new role with a clear mission: transform the platform and the way the company works.

  • Direct work with the founders, reporting to the CEO.

  • A team of about 15 engineers to inherit and reshape.

  • A profitable company moving into Payfac-as-a-Service and embedded distribution.

  • An AI-native setup where non-engineers build their own tools.

  • Year 1 is fixed pay. From year 2, shadow equity tied to P&L performance, with a path to real equity. Details to be agreed.
